articles.title: Sky Tempesta Racing to take part in three Motorsport championships for 2023
articles.summary: "We're excited to announce our participation in the British GT Championship and GT World Challenge Europe in the new McLaren and to continue our partnership with Mercedes in IGTC," said Christopher Froggatt, founder of Sky Tempesta Racing
articles.body:
"We're excited to announce our participation in the Intelligent Money British GT Championship and Fanatec GT World Challenge Europe Powered by AWS Endurance Cup in the new McLaren, and to continue our partnership with Mercedes in IGTC," said Christopher Froggatt, founder of Sky Tempesta Racing.

"Taking on a championship in a new car is always challenging. However, the new McLaren feels great to drive on the track, and we're thrilled to have the expertise of Garage 59 supporting us for both championships in the new car.

"Our team has been working hard to prepare for the upcoming season, and we're looking forward to showing our determination for success this year."

Drivers Chris Froggatt and Kevin Tse will participate in the full Intelligent Money British GT Championship for the first time in the Silver Category.

"I am excited I can finally do a full season in the Intelligent Money British GT championship, and I am delighted to be driving with Sky Tempesta." said Tse.

"I have known Chris for many years. We worked well last year with some success, so we will definitely be looking for multiple podiums this year. Overall, I am thrilled to be able to join the team for the whole season and looking forward to getting on track."

Sky Tempesta's driver line-up of Froggatt, Jonathan Hui and Edward Cheever, who won the 2020 and 2021 Fanatec GT World Challenge Europe Powered by AWS Endurance Cup Pro-Am Championship, said they are looking forward to participating in the Endurance Cup in the Bronze Cup.

"I am very happy to start my fifth season as a Sky Tempesta driver and share the car with two fast and great friends, Chris and Jon," said Cheever.

"We have a history in the Endurance Cup, and although this will be a challenging season for sure, we will do our best to make it a successful one."

"Our team is excited to participate in the Fanatec GT World Challenge Europe Powered by AWS Endurance Championship again," said Froggatt.

"This series is a true test of endurance, teamwork and strategy, and we're confident that the new McLaren, our team at Garage 59, and our drivers will be able to compete at the highest level."

In addition to participating in the Intelligent Money British GT Championship and Fanatec GT World Challenge Europe Powered by AWS Championship, Sky Tempesta Racing will also compete in the IGTC Championship, driving the Mercedes AMG GT3 car, following Hui's success with an impressive class win in the first race of the cup in the LIQUI MOLY Bathurst 12 Hour.

"I am delighted to contest my fifth consecutive season of top-level GT racing with Sky Tempesta. Together we have achieved much success over the past few years, yet, we are hungry as ever for more." said Hui.

"On a personal level, 2023 will be a step into the unknown as I have my eyes on two championships; the IGTC Independent Cup, which got off to a great start with a class win at the Bathurst 12 Hour in the Mercedes AMG GT3 ,and I hope to continue this momentum in the Fanatec GT World Challenge Europe Powered by AWS Cup with the brand new Mclaren 720S GT3 EVO.

"The expectations are high this year, and I will do everything I can to deliver."

articles.title: England Netball: Tracey Neville admits she is 'absolutely not' right choice for head coach job after Jess Thirlby's departure
articles.summary: Tracey Neville admits she does not want England Netball head coach job as she is happy as managing director of Stockport County Women football team; Tamsin Greenway reveals she was not asked if she would want it and later signed a long-term deal at Mavericks
articles.body:
Anna Stembridge will be stepping into the head coach position until after the Commonwealth Games in the summer following Jess Thirlby's decision to quit due to family reasons.

However, after the Games all eyes will be refocusing on the Netball World Cup, held in Sydney from August 25 to September 5, where England could find themselves under new leadership.

"Am I the obvious choice? Of course, I'm the obvious choice," Neville, who last month became managing director of Stockport County Women football team, said on Sky Sports' Off The Court Podcast.

"But am I the right choice? Absolutely not.

"Before I even got the Stockport County Women's job, I've had some great conversations with Sue Campbell [England Netball chair] and Fran Connolly [England Netball CEO].

"And Sue Campbell is very clear about where I am in my career, what my intentions were, and from my perspective now, the challenge I have in my particular role is exactly where I want to be.

"I absolutely love working at Stockport County so she would 100 per cent have known that [returning to England Netball] would not have been the next step."

Neville had been a popular choice to return long before Thirlby's decision was announced, as she was the only coach to lead England to a Commonwealth gold medal before stepping down in 2019 to start a family.

Meanwhile, Greenway, who coaches London Mavericks and would be another popular choice, revealed she was not contacted at all about the decision and believes no coaches in the Netball Super League were spoken to.

"I think maybe my phone's dead or something, there's no reception in London, that's why.

"I don't think there was any phone calls put to any of the current England coaches in the Super League at the moment - I don't believe there was anyway.

"Do I think that should have happened? I don't know. I don't know what the protocol was.

"I don't think anyone saw this coming, I think it's all been a very quick turnaround to whatever's happened."

On Friday it was announced that Greenway had signed a long-term deal with London Mavericks where she will continue to lead the NSL side but also help with the development of the club's performance environment and player pathways.

articles.title: England have selection problem and need more Helen Housby and Liv Tchine support, says Tamsin Greenway
articles.summary: Tamsin Greenway and Tracey Neville discuss England's 'selection problem' in the shooting circle as they call on more support for Helen Housby and Liv Tchine in the latest episode of 'Off The Court', suggesting there are England players that need to play more minutes in Super League.
articles.body:
Speaking on the Off The Court podcast, Greenway and Neville highlighted the eight players they believe are currently assured of a place in the England set-up.

Beyond that, they have questions over the team's depth in the shooting circle and suggested England face a 'selection problem'.

"There is going to be this problem for England selection because if we can only name eight (cemented names) at the minute, it's not like there are a load of players in SSN (Suncorp Super Netball) fighting for it," said former England international Greenway.

"Even in this country we've got players not necessarily playing full games or playing positions they aren't necessarily needed."

England are currently going through a period of adjustment following the shock departure of head coach Jess Thirlby just months out from the Commonwealth Games. Anna Stembridge has stepped into the role ahead of the summer, beyond which the World Cup moves into focus.

"The eight players we talk about being cemented in is Hali Adio, Funmi Fadoju, Fran Williams in the defence end, mid-court Lois Pearson, Jess Shaw and Imogen Allison, and then shooting circle, this is where I think it's a concern, Helen Housby and Liv Tchine.

"Not that they are a concern, but who on earth are we putting into this mix? When you go through the England shooters there are one, two, three, four, five, six that have got their hand up at the minute and I'm looking for that Helen Housby-esque.

"If you aren't playing out in SSN you should be starring every single week in Super League, 60 minutes unless you are 20 goals up and coach is resting you. You should be starring."

Neville pointed towards the duo of Ella Clark and Berri Neil at Loughborough, and so too Nat Metcalf and Eleanor Cardwell at Manchester Thunder as examples of England players competing for minutes at the same position.

"It feels like there is a pressure to play both of them (Clark and Neil)," she said. "We've got the same situation with Nat Metcalf and Eleanor Cardwell, there's a pressure potentially, because Nat Metcalf is going for that Commonwealth Games.

"For me they are not four shooters you would potentially be looking at. You're in a position where you've got all the shooters we would be looking at at the same teams, playing half the games. Is that good enough?

"When I was England coach and I had a player recommendation come to me, my thing was you need a playing percentage time to be able to be competing at the Commonwealth Games. The shooters that used to go would be playing 90-plus minutes for their teams, they were the shooters you'd be going with.

"You need to shoot out when there's pressure, when you're fatigued."

articles.title: Commonwealth Games: Jayda Pechova steps up to Team England senior squad as Nat Metcalf and Fran Williams also named
articles.summary: Team England head coach Anna Stembridge has named a squad of 12 for this summer's Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, scheduled from July 23 to August 2; watch the Netball Super League live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Head coach Anna Stembridge has named a squad of 12, including 2018 Commonwealth champion Metcalf, with Williams set to captain the team for the Glasgow event, scheduled from July 23 to August 2.

Pechova, 21, swept the board at the 2026 Netball Super League awards as she scooped all three individual honours, including Player of the Year.

She becomes the youngest member of the squad and steps up to the senior stage following a stellar campaign for Nottingham Forest.

Pechova earned a brilliant 88 gains and 75 deflections as Forest finished in the top four for the first time in the club's history.

Stembridge, who replaced Jess Thirlby in the role , said: "It is a huge honour to be able to announce the athletes who will represent Team England at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Every player who puts on the red dress understands the responsibility that comes with that opportunity, and the 12 athletes named today have all earned their place through their performances, commitment, and the standards they have shown.

"The competitiveness within English netball is incredibly strong, and this squad reflects the quality and depth we have across the programme. We have a balance of players who bring valuable experience from previous major tournaments, alongside athletes who will be experiencing their first Commonwealth Games and are ready to embrace that opportunity.

"Each athlete brings different qualities to this group, and the strength of this team will come from how we combine those qualities and perform together. We're excited to continue our preparation and represent Team England on one of the biggest stages for our sport."

Williams is one of six players from England's 2023 silver medal-winning World Cup squad who will take to the court this summer, with Liv Tchine also returning and taking on the role of vice-captain alongside Amy Carter.

Goal shooter Tchine heads to her second major international tournament having shone domestically for London Pulse in the Netball Super League (NSL) and on the international stage since her debut in 2022.

Tchine is joined in attack by Eleanor Cardwell, who is selected for her second Commonwealth Games after debuting at Birmingham 2022.

Cardwell's AO Manchester Thunder teammate Lois Pearson, meanwhile, is heading to her first major international competition.

The Bury-born attacker made her international debut in 2024 off the back of a standout NSL season, where she was named Players' Player of the Season, and has continued to be a leading player for club and country since.

Fellow Team England debutant Sasha Glasgow completes the squad's shooting options. Glasgow was born and raised in Australia to English parents and made her international debut in 2023.

In the midcourt, Metcalf returns for her third Games. The wing attack was part of the historic side that won gold at Gold Coast 2018, before she captained Team England at Birmingham 2022 and co-captained the Vitality Roses to a silver medal in the 2023 Netball World Cup. Metcalf returned to court this season following the birth of her daughter, Miller, last year.

She is joined by AO Manchester Thunder teammate Carter, who was a travelling reserve for the 2023 Netball World Cup and captained AO Thunder to a historic fifth NSL title last weekend.

Versatile midcourter Imo Allison is also included for her second Commonwealth Games appearance, having established herself as one of the game's leading players across centre and wing defence.

Jess Shaw completes the midcourt, having impressed in recent domestic seasons with impressive all-action displays. In defence, Williams is joined by Halimat Adio, Funmi Fadoju, and Pechova.

Adio heads to her first Commonwealth Games off the back of a string of strong seasons with London Pulse that have seen her become a mainstay in England's defence.

Fadoju stars alongside Adio for London Pulse and will hope to do the same for Team England at Glasgow 2026.

Defence Halimat Adio (28, London, London Pulse) Francesca Williams (28, Reading, West Coast Fever) Funmi Fadoju (23, Redbridge, London Pulse) Jayda Pechova (21, Fleet, Nottingham Forest)

Midcourt Imo Allison (28, Huddersfield, Queensland Firebirds) Jess Shaw (30, Stockport, Loughborough Lightning) Amy Carter (27, Nottingham, AO Manchester Thunder) Nat Metcalf (33, Keighley, AO Manchester Thunder)

Attack Sasha Glasgow (27, Moonta, Australia, West Coast Fever) Liv Tchine (25, London, London Pulse) Eleanor Cardwell (31, Blackpool, AO Manchester Thunder) Lois Pearson (26, Bury, AO Manchester Thunder)

The Vitality Roses; England Netball's senior team, are currently third in the World Netball world rankings.

Greenway: I'm not sure England can claim gold with 'solid' selection | Neville: It's a safe squad

"It's not a disrespect to anybody that's in that group - you know how much I love Nat Metcalf, she'd be in any of my teams in terms of the experience she brings to leadership, the quality she has on the ball - but again, it's making teams fit.

"It's not about who I'd replace in there because the work had to be done before we got to this point and I think that's what we've harped on about this whole time.

"When I was chatting on that tram on the way back from Manchester and people are just throwing names out and it's like: 'Yeah, but they haven't done it yet so you don't know.'

"Now, that was the problem with Liz Scholes, it was always going to be the problem for Liz Scholes. For me, she would have been in over Jess Shaw in that sense.

"But Jess has been doing the international season so I understand that decision as well.

"I'd take Liz because she is a match winner, and that's my wild card because I'm not sure we can win with solid - and I don't know, this Commonwealth Games is going to be a tough ride.

"It's what we said all the way along. England are capable of finishing gold, they're capable of finishing fifth.

"That's just because of the level of international netball at the minute, there's so many good teams, and it's going to be big-moment players. And I think that's why I'd love to have a little trick up my sleeve to go: 'Go on then kid, go let loose, go and feed some ball in there'."

Sky Sports Netball's Tracey Neville - former England international and head coach - added:

"I actually knew that Nat Metcalf would get in there just generally for the experience.

"It's a safe England squad. Probably what we predicted.

"It would have been interesting if Helen Housby would have been available, what that change up would have been. Would it have been a Nat [Metcalf] or a Sasha [Glasgow] who would have lost their place? Who knows?

"But yeah, I didn't expect anything else."

England star Housby ruled out of Commonwealth Games

In April it was revealed that Housby would miss an "extended period" of the Suncorp Super Netball season in Australia due to a back injury, with further scans confirming she will be unable to compete this summer.

Housby, who famously scored England's last-minute winner when they won gold at the 2018 Commonwealth Games, says she is "devastated" to miss out in the Glasgow event.

Representing Team England is an honour and holds some of my proudest and fondest memories," she said.

"Despite the setback I'm more determined than ever to come back stronger and get back on court as soon as possible, especially with the World Cup in Sydney on the horizon.

"I'm lucky to be surrounded by an incredible support system and I'm very grateful for the love I've received from those closest to me, England Netball, the New South Wales Swifts and the Vitality Roses fans back home.

"I'm excited to see what our girls can achieve this summer and will be giving everything I can off the court to support them in Glasgow. I truly believe our squad can beat anybody and I'm looking forward to watching as a fan this time around."

articles.title: Women's World Matchplay: Beau Greaves defeats Fallon Sherrock in 6-5 last-leg decider to claim record third Blackpool crown
articles.summary: Beau Greaves came out on top against Fallon Sherrock with a 6-5 victory; it is a record-extending third Blackpool win; you can watch the World Matchplay final live on Sky Sports Action and Sky Sports Main Event from 7.30pm in Blackpool
articles.body:
After Sherrock forced the contest the distance, Greaves held her nerve with a crucial 180 before a brilliant 145 left 56 for the title. She coolly pinned double 10 to seal victory once again.

The win adds to Greaves' 2023 and 2024 triumphs in this tournament. It was Sherrock that Greaves met in the 2024 Women's Matchplay final in which Greaves took the spoils in a 6-3 win.

It adds to an already impressive year for 'Beau and Arrow' in which she became the first woman to win a Pro Tour event at Players Championship 11. She also hit a nine-darter on the Tour and became the first woman to qualify for the European Tour.

The win for Greaves consigns Sherrock to runner-up at the Women's Matchplay for a third year in a row, losing to Greaves in 2024 and 2026 plus Lisa Ashton in 2025.

"I'm not one to celebrate but it was relief in the end. Fallon is a great lass and an even better darts player. I knew I had to play well but to hit that last dart was an outpouring of relief," Greaves told Sky Sports .

"Just so happy to win. I knew playing the women is a bit different because I play the men now. Chuffed just to get the win.

"I was nervous, but that kind of pressure is a privilege.

"I just love my life. love playing darts. I can't get enough of it. I'm addicted to it in a way and just love my life and even supporting the women's game is a massive thing.

"I love darts and it's good enough for me. My goal is to just play better."

It was billed as a close and enthralling contest between the two most successful players in women's darts, and it certainly lived up to expectations on the Winter Gardens stage.

Sherrock made the brighter start to the final, breaking throw in the third leg. But, in typical Greaves fashion, she hit back immediately to restore parity at 2-2 before producing a sensational 120 checkout in a 12-dart leg to move ahead.

From there, the contest developed into a gripping nip-and-tuck affair. A tense eighth leg eventually went Greaves' way as she pinned double two to secure a crucial break of throw and move within one leg of the title.

Sherrock, however, refused to go down without a fight. Some superb scoring left her on 36 after just nine darts, and she wrapped up an 11-dart break of throw. She then followed it with a classy 70 checkout on double 16 to force a deciding leg

That was when Greaves found her brilliant best once again with a maximum then silky 145 leaving her 56 for the title. On 56, she took double 10 to ensure the trophy was coming home with her.

Greaves' route to final: Brilliance and a battle!

Greaves had to battle hard to make it into the final in a 5-4 nerve-wracking victory over Gemma Hayter.

Greaves got off to slow start and Hayter made sure to capitalise, levelling the game at 2-2 with a break of throw on tops and then finding another crucial break with an 83 checkout on double 16 to take the game to a last-leg decider.

However, just when she needed it, Greaves came through with a massive 104 checkout to book her spot in a third Women's Matchplay final.

Greaves made it through to the semi-finals with a 5-1 victory over Kirsi Viinikainen, starting in imperious fashion with a 148 then 144 checkout to get the contest going.

Sherrock route to the final: One leg dropped!

Ashton's title defence came to an end when she ran into a clinical Sherrock who pulled off a 5-1 win to make her third straight Matchplay final in a row.

Indeed, it was a replay of the 2025 Matchplay final, but this time Greaves was firmly in control. Having dropped just a single leg en route to the final, she sealed her place in the showpiece match by pinning double 16.

Sherrock was also at her brilliant best in a 5-0 whitewash victory over Deta Hedman in the quarters, two 13-darters in a row the key as she gave the 'Caribbean Queen' no opportunities to counter attack and zero darts at the double.

Elsewhere, Hayter battled from 4-2 down to win a last-leg shootout against Vicky Pruim, overcoming some key errors to eventually pin a clutch 77 on tops for the match.

Meanwhile, the 'Lancashire Rose' Ashton began with a 5-2 win over Welsh No 1 Rhian O'Sullivan, a big 120 checkout for a break of throw the highlight before she eventually clinched the game with her ninth match dart.

What is happening in the men's World Matchplay?

The 2026 Betfred World Matchplay continues at the iconic Winter Gardens on Sunday night, as defending champion Luke Littler takes on Gerwyn Price for the prestigious Phil Taylor Trophy.

articles.title: Luke Littler hails World Matchplay defence as one of the 'best weeks of his life' after historic Gerwyn Price victory
articles.summary: Luke Littler became the first player in a decade to defend his title at the World Matchplay; he broke the record for the most 180s hit in the tournament and set the highest-ever average recorded in a final with 111.53
articles.body:
It capped off a week in which Littler has broken record after record. The 19-year-old started his week with a 109 average against Niko Springer and then took things to new heights with a 113 average and nine-darter against Nathan Aspinall.

A 109 average against Josh Rock followed, before he demolished Dirk van Duijvenbode in the semi-finals.

Littler then became the first player in a decade to retain the title at the Winter Gardens, defeating Price while rewriting the record books in the process.

Littler fired an 111.53 average which smashed the tournament scoring record, previously set by Phil Taylor in 2010, leaving Littler continuing his run of winning every PDC TV major in 2026.

He also posted six ton-plus finishes and broke his own tournament record for most 180s, hitting 66 across the week.

Not only that, he broke the £3m earning barrier during his run to the final, with the latest win enhancing his hopes of sweeping every ranked major in a calendar year.

They are numbers to simply behold and Littler himself counts them as some of the best he has ever posted in his life.

"It has been a crazy week - it has been one of the best weeks of my life," Littler told Sky Sports .

"The darts I have played - it has not been easy. It has been tough. The stats may look like it is easy but when you are on this stage, it is hot, it is not easy.

"I have played some of the best darts of my life.

"Two years ago, I had that first round defeat to Michael which was not the best result, The last two years, I have come here with the family and we have done it again.

"It is definitely, I feel like it is the best version of myself. I have just been playing so well.

Littler said on the opening night of the World Matchplay that, if he defended his title, he would then have to head to the Pro Tour in order to attempt the clean sweep which would include having to defend his Players Championship Finals win in Minehead.

With that in mind, the world No 1's next stop is Leicester, rather than the planned trip to Spain.

"I don't think my dad is too happy because we were meant to be going to Spain but now we will be going to Leicester for some Pro Tours," he added.

"Coming into the tournament I had won every major so far so this is what I wanted to do.

"I have been checking the Pro Tour rankings. I know there is four in Leicester I have got to go to now.

"If I don't qualify I will get grilled, if I qualify I will get grilled anyway so who knows what is going to happen."

The next PDC ranked TV major is the BoyleSports World Grand Prix from September 28-October 4 at the Mattioli Arena, Leicester, live on Sky Sports . Littler returns as defending champion after last year's victory over Luke Humphries in the double in, double out event.

The Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton (November 14-22) and the World Darts Championship (December 10-January 3) are also both live on Sky Sports, with Littler looking to retain his titles in both events. Stream darts and more top sport with no contract.

articles.title: Commonwealth Games: England fight back to beat South Africa and reach netball semi-finals at Glasgow 2026
articles.summary: In a winner-takes-all group match to progress to the semi-finals, England came out on top against South Africa to secure a place in the last four; England overcame an early deficit to maintain their 100 per cent record of reaching the semi-finals at the Commonwealth Games
articles.body:
Both sides needed to win to book a spot in the last four and England roared back from an early 17-11 deficit after the first quarter to keep their hopes of a second Commonwealth gold alive.

The Vitality Roses will face New Zealand in the second of Saturday's semi-finals after Australia play Jamaica, then the gold and bronze-medal matches take place on Sunday.

"Shout out to Halimat Adio. She was unreal in that second quarter. So proud of her to bring us that energy and get us back in the game when we needed it," captain Francesca Williams told TNT Sports .

"We have been under pressure all week to perform so for us to finish out a game like that and ride the wave of goal for goal in the last quarter and come out on top, I'm so proud."

England got off to a nervy start as South Africa goal shooter Elmere van der Berg came flying out of the blocks with 16 goals from 19 attempts which silenced the crowd at the OVO Hydro.

Halimat Adio and Funmi Fadoju came on, which tightened up England's defence, and it changed the momentum of the match as they slowly got themselves back into the contest to trail just 29-28 at half-time.

England went on a charge early in the third quarter with five consecutive goals to move 35-30 ahead and took a 45-41 lead into the last quarter.

As the clock ran down, England calmly maintained their slender four-goal advantage as Olivia Tchine and Lois Pearson kept their composure up front to get Anna Stembridge's side over the line.

Stembridge stepped up to become head coach just four months before the Commonwealth Games after Jess Thirlby resigned.

Netball has been in the Commonwealth Games since 1998 but England have never won a medal when it has been held in the United Kingdom.

articles.title: Hungarian Darts Trophy: Ross Smith defeats Gary Anderson as Scot's fairy-tale run ends in final
articles.summary: Ross Smith thrashed Gary Anderson 8-2 in the final of the Hungarian Darts Trophy at Budapest's MVM Dome; the 2022 European champion averaged 101 to claim a second European Tour title of the year; Anderson had survived five match darts just to reach the decider
articles.body:
Smith averaged 101 and converted 73 per cent of his attempts at a double in a near-flawless closing display at the MVM Dome, giving Anderson no way back into a contest that slipped away from the veteran almost immediately and sealing a fourth win of the day for the champion.

Smith had been the tournament's model of scoring control from the first day of his involvement, opening with a 101 average against William O'Connor that featured 116 and 112 checkouts.

He then saw off fourth seed Jonny Clayton 6-4 in the last 16 before dismantling 2023 champion Dave Chisnall 6-2 in a quarter-final that guaranteed a first-time winner of this title.

His semi-final was the most one-sided match of the weekend's business end, with last year's runner-up Danny Noppert swept aside 7-3 in a clinical display that gave Smith the fresher legs for the final.

Anderson's run, although he was vanquished in the final, ends as the story of the weekend all the same.

The two-time world champion had arrived in Budapest without a European Tour win in 2026 and opened with a statement, a 105.27 average in a 6-2 dismantling of Krzysztof Ratajski that ended the Pole's bid for back-to-back European Tour titles.

What followed was an escalating sequence of escapes.

Anderson hit eight 180s in recovering from 3-0 down to edge eighth seed Stephen Bunting in a deciding leg, then repeated the trick against second seed Gian van Veen in a quarter-final thriller.

The Scottish veteran then won the match of the tournament against Nathan Aspinall, staring down five match darts in a 7-6 epic and conjuring a 160 checkout simply to stay alive, before the final proved one test too many.

The title decider crowned a finals day of upsets that began with Aspinall knocking out Michael van Gerwen 6-4 in the last 16, recovering from 3-1 down in a match of nervy doubles to end the 2024 champion's bid for a second crown.

That came a day after top seed Luke Humphries and defending champion Niko Springer had fallen , meaning the tournament's past two winners both exited before the final session.

Aspinall's weekend, prior to meeting Anderson, was a study in finding a way through matches where he couldn't find his best form. Out-averaged by Ryan Joyce in his opening match, he came through on five 180s and sheer volume of chances at a double – and his quarter-final against Chris Dobey turned on a 156 checkout before he edged another deciding leg.

Dobey had comebacks of his own to look back on, recovering from 4-0 down to beat Tom Sykes in a decider on Saturday before closing Sunday's afternoon session by reeling in a 170 finish to see off sixth seed Josh Rock 6-3.

Dirk van Duijvenbode ended a nine-match losing run against Humphries on Saturday and was the first man into the quarter-finals, beating Rob Cross 6-4 to end the former world champion's run of successive deciding-leg escapes, before Noppert halted him 6-5.

Springer's title defence had lasted just 14 minutes against Ryan Searle on Saturday, the German missing the bull for a 164 that would have forced a decider, and with Humphries, Van Gerwen and Clayton also gone by Sunday afternoon, Van Veen stood as the highest seed left until Anderson took him out too.

articles.title: Czech Darts Open: Luke Littler topples Luke Humphries 8-6 in final on return to European Tour in Prague
articles.summary: Littler beats Humphries 8-6 in final after beating Michael van Gerwen, Danny Noppert and Krzysztof Ratajski earlier on Sunday; Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the World Grand Prix coming up from September 28-October 4
articles.body:
Littler had not played in a European Tour event since March, but roared to glory with an 8-6 victory in Sunday night's final to end his opponent's hopes of winning this title for a third straight year.

Littler hit five 180s and averaged just over 95 as both players struggled in the heat at the PVA EXPO after a long day which had already seen The Nuke overcome Michael van Gerwen in the semi-finals, Danny Noppert in the quarter-finals and Krzysztof Ratajski in the last 16.

"It's good to be back and I'm back with a bang," said Littler after his victory.

World No 1 Littler won the first two legs against world No 2 Humphries in Sunday's final, only to see his rival, who has reached four of the last five finals in this tournament, reel off three straight legs to take the lead.

Littler fought back to move ahead with a 130 checkout in the ninth leg - the biggest finish of the game - and then won the next two legs to move 7-4 ahead in a race to eight.

Humphries rallied to win the next two legs and was millimetres away from sending the game to a decider, as he wired two darts at D16.

Littler recovered to pin D10 to win this tournament for the first time, taking home the £35,000 first prize and guaranteeing his place at the European Championship in Dortmund in October.

That's one of the titles that Littler wants to win as he eyes a clean sweep of major trophies in 2026 - and it means he's unlikely to play in any other regular European Tour events this season.

"I'm not sure now I've won this one," he explained. "I think I've secured my place in Dortmund. That's obviously the one I'm chasing.

"In two weeks time it's the World Series in Amsterdam. We'll have to see what happens, what the plan is and how busy I am."

Humphries had overcome Gerwyn Price, William O'Connor and Andrew Gilding earlier on Sunday to reach the final for the third year in a row, but he was not upset at missing out on a 'three-peat'.

"I can't be upset," he said. "The two darts I threw at D16 were right on the wire and if that goes in, it could have been a different game.

"That's just the way it goes. He's a fantastic player. I've been playing here and there, not so great. Maybe good sometimes. I've got to dedicate my life a bit more to get better and keep pushing him.

"I keep saying I'm not beating him in finals so I've got to change things to keep matching him.

"I think he enjoys the challenge and I love it as well. Hopefully over the next four months, I push him and if he does the clean sweep [of major titles] he has to do it the hard way."

articles.title: Super League: Wakefield Trinity beat Leigh Leopards to earn play-offs rematch as Warrington Wolves set up Hull KR clash
articles.summary: Warrington Wolves finished in third with their win and now will face Hull KR in the Eliminators; Wakefield Trinity and Leigh Leopards will clash again in the other Eliminator contest; The Super League play-offs begin on Friday September 18, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The two sides will clash again next week in the fourth vs fifth Eliminator contest but this time the contest will take place in Yorkshire on Friday September 18, live on Sky Sports .

The fourth-place finish is Wakefield's highest ever in the Super League season and is the latest sign of their resurgence under Daryl Powell after returning to the Super League in 2025.

Meanwhile, a 26-14 win for a young Warrington Wolves side over Toulouse Olympique saw them wrap up third spot and they will face Hull KR, who finished in sixth after a 36-12 loss to St Helens. That match will take place on Saturday September 19, also live on Sky Sports .

The winners of those two contests will then advance to the semi-finals for the chance to face either League Leaders' Shield winners Wigan Warriors or second-place Leeds Rhinos for a spot in the Grand Final at Old Trafford on October 3.

Wakefield make statement as Leigh cannot finish fight back

In the warm-up for the Eliminator match-up between Wakefield and Leigh Leopards, Tom Johnstone went over early for the visitors as they made the most of their own kick, Jake Trueman sending his winger sliding in for a 4-0 lead.

Two Max Jowitt penalties then came alongside a second try for the Wakefield winger that was the most spectacular of finishes, moving them 12-0 up.

Trueman then sent a message just before the break as he sent over a drop goal for a 13-0 advantage, the home Leigh faithful sombre knowing this was the exact contest they will play next week away from home.

Leigh Leopards came out chancing their arm in the second half and Owen Trout got them on the scoreboard.

It then looked like they were heading towards a comeback after Mason Lino was sent to the sin bin for a professional foul and they capitalised through Innes Senior with a brilliant finish on the edge to bring the score to 13-8.

However, Wakefield stood strong and with just three minutes left on the clock, Cam Scott powered over in the corner and Jowitt converted to wrap up a 19-8 win.

Leigh beat Wakefield in the play-offs in 2025 but if they are to do it again, it would mark their first win over Trinity this season.

Powell: It is time for us to show we are good enough

Wakefield Trinity head coach Daryl Powell speaking to Sky Sports...

"I thought the boys did us proud today. We had a sin-binning but then we were tough and courageous after that.

"We will dust ourselves down, learn from this, and get ready.

"I think both teams will have been talking about it being around play-off time and being ready for it.

"We probably left a couple of points on the field thanks to some desperate defence from Leigh.

"It is all about next week now. Leigh beat us last year in the play-offs, we were stinging from that, and we carried that into this year."

"I just think we have had some great lessons," he added.

"We have carried them through with us and we are a better team for having them at the end of the season.

"It is awesome- into the six and a great opportunity for us.

"Are we good enough? It is for us to show we are. It is for us to show we are capable of great things."

Warrington head coach Sam Burgess took a risk to rest the majority of his side, having made 11 changes, and opted for his young guns to see his side home in third position, and they did just that with a gusty victory.

Toulouse have impressed across 2026 under Sylvain Houles on their return to Super League and early on they had Warrington locked into a contest.

They went over first through Paul Ulberg, but an error on their own line allowed Aaron Lindop to capitalise.

The visitors hit back again through Mathieu Pons but on the stroke of half-time, Lachlan Webster levelled at 8-8. None of the four tries scored were converted.

Similarly to the first half, Toulouse were the first to go over again in the second period thanks to Romeo Tropis, but then Warrington took things up a notch.

After Max Wood barged over from short range, Lindop capitalised on another error for his second.

Even with a man down after Charlie McKler was sent to the sin bin for a high shot, the Wolves showed their grit and Josh Smith did incredibly to slide in on the end of a Leon Hayes kick.

Hayes converted three of the five efforts and Warrington now have Hull KR in their sights as they welcome them to the Halliwell Jones Stadium in a clash for a spot in the semi-finals.

Saints bid farewell to two modern legends as KR finish sixth

It was an emotional night in St Helens as they said goodbye to two modern-day legends, Mark Percival and Jonny Lomax, and they marked it with a 36-12 victory over Hull KR, who finish the season in sixth place.

They handed the former the captaincy for the first time in his career, a guard of honour forming as the pair made their way out onto the field.

However, their farewells also marked their earliest goodbye to a season in their history; after finishing seventh and taking on an inexperienced Hull KR side, they were expected to finish with a sizeable victory.

The Robins had welcomed back Mikey Lewis from his two-match ban but head coach Willie Peters had opted to rest his players ahead of the defence of their title.

The first half was written in the stars for the home side as Percival opened the scoring, then provided the assist for Lomax to mark Saints' second.

Just when you thought the storyline was done, Lomax barged over for his second on the stroke of half-time for an 18-0 lead.

Hull KR did hit back through Bill Leyland and a sensational solo effort from 18-year-old Flynn Holden on debut, but efforts from Deon Cross, Jacob Host, and Harry Robertson were enough to seal the comprehensive win as an era came to a fitting end at Saints.

articles.title: 2026 Super League Dream Team: Leeds Rhinos lead with six inclusions, with Wigan, Wakefield, Warrington, Leigh, Toulouse represented
articles.summary: The 13 players included in the Super League Dream Team for 2026 have been revealed: Leeds Rhinos have six inclusions, Leigh and Wigan have two each: Toulouse, Warrington, and Wakefield also represented Super League play-offs begin on September 18, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The Dream Team was selected through three elements, combining the views of the Man of Steel panel (50% per cent), a selected group of Rugby League journalists (30 per cent), and Super League fans (20%).

The conclusion of the vote saw six Leeds players chosen along with two Wigan Warriors players, two Leigh Leopards players, plus a player each from Wakefield Trinity, Warrington Wolves, and Toulouse Olympique.

Such low representation for the Warriors may come as a surprise given that they have already wrapped up a domestic double and are on the hunt for the treble if they reach the Grand Final.

Brad Arthur's Rhinos were flying high throughout the majority of the season until they faltered against Matt Peet's side and ultimately finished second.

Four players in the team have been included before, with the other nine making their first appearance.

Let's take a look at who has been chosen as the best of the best across the regular Super League season in 2026...

Miller has lit up Super League in 2026, really hitting his stride in the fullback position.

He was top of the Man of Steel standings for the opening nine rounds and was right in the mix for the second third of the season too.

Unfortunately, Miller has suffered a season-ending hamstring injury, which will leave all fans wondering just how much influence he could have had for Leeds in the play-offs.

His link-ups with his half-backs have been electrifying to watch and his pace means he is a mean feat to stop in broken play.

Wigan's Jai Field has also been strong in the fullback role, but in 2026, Miller has been chosen as the competition's most consistent.

Wingers: Maika Sivo (Leeds Rhinos) and Zack Eckersley (Wigan Warriors)

On the wings, we have a try-scoring phenom and a youngster who has had a year to remember in which his career has truly been set alight.

Before suffering his forearm injury at the end of July in round 20, Maika Sivo was scoring at a freakish rate and finishes as Super League's top try scorer with 29 tries.

It is a symbol in itself that he missed six rounds of action and still finished top.

Eckersley, meanwhile, has excelled on the wing for Wigan this year and has been making metres for his team at some rate.

He has 27 tries to his name, just two less than Sivo, but has developed into a winger that Wigan can truly rely on in all facets of their game.

Centres: Ash Handley (Leeds Rhinos) and Umyla Hanley (Leigh Leopards)

In the centres, Ash Handley and Umyla Hanley take the spoils.

Hanley has played just 16 games this season, but since coming back from his injury has been in unbelievable form, which has earned him a call-up to the England squad ahead of the World Cup.

Adam Keighran of the Warriors has also been in great form in that same spot but it is the Leigh man who has shone and earned back-to-back inclusions in the Dream Team.

His head coach Adrian Lam described him as the most "fierce" competitor he has met and he has shown that in spades.

Handley has been the dominant force in the centres for the majority of the season.

The captain of the Rhinos, with his sheer dominance and power, coupled with his speed, has been very hard to stop in 2026.

We said that the Leeds spine has been particularly interwoven in 2026 and that sees Brodie Croft included at stand off.

Remarkably, Croft finishes in second place for try scorers with 28, just one behind his winger Sivo.

He has been there, popping up at every opportunity to get points on the board for his side and makes a return to the Dream Team for the first time in four years.

And the final piece of that Leeds spine puzzle- reigning Man of Steel Jake Connor. He has been the man with all the assists in 2026 and it is back-to-back inclusions for him too.

Connor provided 43 assists across the season. To put into perspective how remarkable a stat that is, second-placed Jackson Hastings provided 29- 14 less than the leader.

His kicking game has also been pivotal for Leeds across this year and now he will want to turn that consistency into big game action.

It is worth a word here for Harry Smith, who has had a really strong year and was also a notable candidate at scrum half.

A near constant presence for Wigan in 2026, Brad O'Neill has been the main lieutenant in the defensive steel of a Wigan outfit that look primed to win it all.

His defensive efforts are second to none; his aggression has become much more measured, and he has cemented himself as the standout hooker across the year.

Wakefield's Tyson Smoothy has also impressed in the role but O'Neill has been the general in a well-oiled machine and it is the mark of an exceptional player that a team's performance dips when he is not on the field.

Props: Caleb Hamlin-Uele (Wakefield Trinity) and Joe Ofahengaue (Leigh Leopards)

Caleb Hamlin-Uele has been a near-constant member of a Wakefield side that wrapped up their highest Super League finish in their history and his metre-making has been a sight to behold.

Called up to the England squad ahead of the World Cup, Hamlin-Uele has been a stalwart in defence but also given his side go forward when it mattered.

The same can be said of Joe Ofahengaue, who has been arguably Leigh's best player across the year. His gains for his team are right at the top and not only that, he provides an offload threat that means the attack never feels over when he has the ball in hand.

Back Row: James McDonnell (Leeds Rhinos) and Mathieu Jussaume (Toulouse Olympique)

There is a bit of history in the back row as Mathieu Jussaume's inclusion means he is the first-ever Toulouse Olympique player to make the Dream Team.

He has been a solid and key member of the defensive line, especially when it comes to marker tackles, but he also carries incredibly well and makes sure to open up the attack for his side.

James McDonnell, meanwhile, is the fourth repeat inclusion with Connor, Croft, and Hanley. McDonnell was also in the 2025 Dream Team.

The Leeds man has been the definition of consistent for the Rhinos and does the hard yards incredibly well.

It is noticed when he is not on the field and Leeds always look stronger when he is carrying the ball hard.

There are worthy shout-outs for Junior Nsemba and Isaiah Vagana who have impressed in the same position.

Loose Forward: Ben Currie (Warrington Wolves)

Finally, Warrington Wolves' Ben Currie is in at loose forward after a standout year for the third-place finishers.

Currie is right up there in tackles made this season, marker tackles too, and has been the constant and consistent member of Sam Burgess' side. A talisman, if you will.

He has been the epitome of a leader and deservedly makes the Dream Team.

I imagine Oli Partington was right up there in the votes too after a sensational year for Wigan.

articles.title: Leigh Leopards and Wakefield Trinity ready for rematch as both clubs look to make more history
articles.summary: Leigh Leopards and Wakefield Trinity will do play-off battle once again for a spot in the semi-finals; watch Wakefield Trinity vs Leigh Leopards in the Super League Eliminators, live on Sky Sports on Friday September 18, with kick-off at 8pm
articles.body:
Wakefield made history with a fourth-placed finish in Super League, the highest in the club's history. Next on the list is reaching the semi-finals for the first time.

Leigh, meanwhile, have been making waves since their return to the top flight in 2023, winning the Challenge Cup and making the Super League semi-finals regularly.

The next step for them is making it all the way to the big dance.

For Joe Ofahengaue, to do that, the Leopards need to execute their game plan well. If they do, they might just achieve the very thing that would mean "everything".

"It was a weird one. I thought the game shaped out to be all in Wakefield's favour," Ofahengaue told Sky Sports .

"That is not directing anything at the way the game was reffed. I just think we got our game plan wrong.

"They executed on a few mishaps in our defence but the gods of rugby league have looked after us and given us a second shot.

"I think if we get our game plan on, we can really make some noise in this play-offs.

"Making it to the Grand Final would mean everything. I am banking on it.

"I am very emotionally attached to this squad. We have some key members of this squad leaving after this year and I want to send them out on a high note.

"The only way we can send them out on a high is if we win it.

"I don't want to look too for ahead or picture myself too far ahead but it is definitely a great goal of ours to reach Old Trafford."

Powell: We want to be genuine contenders

Wakefield head coach Daryl Powell has been integral to the club hitting new heights, getting better and better every season.

They were only promoted back to Super League in 2025, finishing sixth, and now moving up to fourth, is a symbol that they are growing into a club that consistently challenges at the top.

The next symbol for them is making it wins against Leigh two weeks in a row.

"I would expect Leigh to step up intensity-wise," Powell told Sky Sports .

"I think they will go to another level. I mentioned that to the boys, I don't think you can expect that game to dictate anything that happens this week.

"We have just got to reset ourselves, go again, and we feel like we can play better actually.

"We are talking about progression each year. We finished sixth and we didn't feel like we did ourselves justice in the play-off game against Leigh in 2025.

"It's ironic that we face them again this year and a chance for a little bit of redemption. Being a genuine top-four team is about getting to those semi-finals and giving yourself a chance to get to the Grand Final.

"It would be an awesome thing for the club. If we can do that, we will be pretty excited."

articles.title: Why Suchika Tariyal lost despite a draw: How 700g denied India’s MMA fighter a historic final and left her in tears
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: The medal will go down in Indian sporting history. The manner in which it arrived, however, left Suchika Tariyal in tears.Twenty-four years.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The medal will go down in Indian sporting history. The manner in which it arrived, however, left Suchika Tariyal in tears.Twenty-four years after an episode of eve-teasing at the age of 12 prompted her to learn how to fight, the 36-year-old from Haryana became India's first Asian Games medallist in mixed martial arts on Monday. But instead of walking away celebrating a landmark achievement, Tariyal was left shattered on the mat after a dramatic semifinal ended in a draw — only for the winner to be determined by a 700-gram difference in the fighters' morning weights.Tariyal and Singapore's Hui Hoon Teo had fought through regulation time and an additional one-minute round without either establishing a decisive advantage. The bout was initially awarded to Teo. The Indian camp challenged the decision, after which the result was changed to a draw.Then came the tiebreak.MMA Sports Federation president Nikhil Kunde told PTI that the winner was determined on the basis of the athletes' morning weigh-in, with Teo around 700 grams lighter than Tariyal. The Singaporean was therefore declared the winner 2-0 and advanced to the gold-medal bout, while Tariyal received bronze.For Tariyal, it was a particularly painful way for her gold-medal hopes to end.She had believed she had done enough to win. Teo had the better of the opening period, but Tariyal fought back strongly in the second. Neither could establish clear superiority in the additional round, although Tariyal managed to take her opponent down just as the buzzer sounded.When the final decision was announced, Tariyal struggled to contain her emotions. She broke down in tears on the mat as her coach tried to console her. She did not immediately go across to shake hands with Teo or the referee.The disappointment was understandable. A few moments earlier, the Indian camp had succeeded in getting the initial verdict changed to a draw. Yet the revised result still did not take Tariyal into the final. A difference of roughly 700 grams ultimately separated the two fighters.And yet, history had already been made.MMA is making its Asian Games debut at Aichi-Nagoya 2026, and Tariyal's bronze is India's first-ever medal in the discipline. Her achievement also adds another chapter to one of the most unusual combat-sports journeys in the Indian contingent.From an incident at 12 to the Asian Games podiumTariyal's journey into combat sports began not with dreams of an Asian Games medal, but with a desire for self-defence.At 12, after experiencing eve-teasing, she decided she wanted to learn how to fight. She took up judo and gradually transformed that initial need for protection into a competitive sporting career.Judo became her foundation. She trained at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium and later at the Dada Dev Mandir Centre in Palam before honing her skills at the Sports Authority of India centre in Bhopal.The journey eventually produced eight national judo titles and international success. She won gold at the 2019 Commonwealth Judo Championships and the 2019 South Asian Games, besides winning silver at the 2018 Commonwealth Judo Championships. She represented India at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham in the women's 57kg category, narrowly missing a medal.But judo was only the beginning.Tariyal moved into kurash and represented India at the 2023 Asian Games. She also took up Ju-Jitsu, eventually becoming world champion in the Adults Ju-Jitsu Contact Female 63kg category at the 2024 JJIF Ju-Jitsu World Championships.Her relationship with MMA had begun earlier, with a debut victory in 2017. She then spent seven years away from the sport while continuing her career in other combat disciplines.When she returned to professional MMA in 2024, she did so with the experience of a fighter who had already spent years building different parts of her game.She made her professional comeback at BRAVE CF 92 in Bahrain in December 2024 and won. Her subsequent MMA career included national titles and bronze medals at the Asian Mixed Martial Arts Championships in 2026.That multi-discipline background became central to her Asian Games campaign.Judo, Ju-Jitsu and MMA come togetherTariyal's MMA style was built around the skills she had accumulated over the years — takedowns, grappling, ground control and submissions.Before the Asian Games, she underwent a six-week preparation camp in Mumbai under coaches Nikhil and Sushobhan. She had spoken about how her coaches would wait for her through Mumbai's traffic so she could complete her training and continue refining her techniques.Her preparation showed when she stepped into the Asian Games cage.In Sunday's quarterfinal, Tariyal defeated Mongolia's Altanchimeg Baigalmaa 2-0 in the women's traditional 60kg category to reach the semifinals. The victory guaranteed India its first medal in MMA because both losing semifinalists received bronze.It was a moment Tariyal had waited years for.“It took me a lot of time to reach here. There is a lot of hard work -- first judo, then other games and now MMA,” she had said after reaching the last four.On Monday, she came within one step of turning that historic bronze into a shot at gold.Instead, the semifinal became a contest decided not simply by what happened inside the cage, but by what the morning weigh-in showed.A historic medal, with a bitter aftertasteThere is no taking away what Tariyal has accomplished.She has become India's first Asian Games MMA medallist at an edition in which the sport itself is making its debut. At 36, she has added another major milestone to a career that has crossed judo, kurash, Ju-Jitsu and professional MMA.But the circumstances of the semifinal mean the bronze is unlikely to feel complete to her immediately.The Indian challenge had changed the original decision. The bout had become a draw. Over the years, she has become one of the most dependable figures in Indian women’s hockey, featuring at three Olympic Games, two Asian Games, the Commonwealth Games, and several Asian Champions Trophy and FIH Pro League campaigns.She also served as captain of the Indian women’s team before Salima Tete took over the role.Savita reached her 300th international appearance in February 2025 against the Netherlands in the FIH Hockey Pro League. She became only the second Indian woman, after Vandana, to reach the milestone, and the second Indian goalkeeper, after PR Sreejesh, to do so.Savita surpasses Vandana Katariya’s recordSavita equalled Vandana’s record of 320 appearances on September 20, 2026, during India’s 19-0 win over Uzbekistan in their Asian Games opener. She then moved past the mark in Monday’s match against Indonesia.Vandana, India’s all-time leading goal-scorer, made her international debut in the same year as Savita and retired in April 2025 after 320 appearances and 158 goals. articles.title: ¿Por qué un Ferrari comprado en 2015 por 300.000 euros puede venderse hoy por 1,5 millones?
articles.standfirst: Con solo 1.134 kilómetros desde su entrega en 2015, este 458 Speciale Aperta, del que solo hay 499 unidades, sale a subasta y los expertos esperan un precio de escándalo.
articles.summary: Con solo 1.134 kilómetros desde su entrega en 2015, este 458 Speciale Aperta, del que solo hay 499 unidades, sale a subasta y los expertos esperan un precio de escándalo.
articles.body: Un coleccionista particular ha decidido desprenderse del Ferrari 458 Speciale Aperta que compró en 2015. Hasta ahí, todo entra dentro de lo normal. Lo curioso es que desde entonces solo le ha hecho 1.134 kilómetros, y eso, en el mundo del coleccionismo, contribuye a que el precio que se estima que alcance cuando sea subastado este próximo 23 de septiembre será de entre 1.000.000 y 1.500.000 de euros. En este híper precio influye el hecho de que no se trata 'solo' de un Ferrari 458 descapotable. El 458 Spider, la variante abierta del modelo estándar, entregaba 570 CV, mientras que la Speciale Aperta parte de la mecánica de la versión más agresiva del 458, la Speciale, con 605 CV a 9.000 rpm, aerodinámica activa con aletas que cambian de posición, un sistema de control de deslizamiento pionero para su época y suspensión y dirección afinadas para exprimir el trazado de Fiorano o aquel que tenga más cerca su afortunado propietario. Además, el hecho de que sea descapotable añade apenas 50 kg al conjunto respecto al cupé, un logro de ingeniería espectacular. Pero si está tan cotizado no es más tanto por el incremento de potencia, sino sobre todo porque Ferrari fabricó solo 499 unidades de este Speciale Aperta, presentado en el Salón de París de 2014. Es decir, se trata de la variante más escasa de toda la familia 458, más incluso que el propio Speciale cupé, del que se estiman varios miles de unidades pese a tratarse también de una serie especial. Y hay un matiz que dispara todavía más su atractivo entre coleccionistas, se trata del último Ferrari de motor central trasero con un V8 de aspiración natural, y también del último de ese tipo diseñado por Pininfarina antes de que la firma italiana pusiera fin a su colaboración de décadas con Maranello en los modelos de motor central. Para seguir entiendo el porqué de su precio, esta unidad añade una configuración que se aparta de lo habitual en el modelo. La mayoría de los Speciale Aperta se vistieron por dentro con Alcantara, el material preferido por Ferrari para sus versiones más orientadas a pista, pero este ejemplar luce un habitáculo completo en piel Bordeaux, cinturones y volante incluidos, combinado con una carrocería en Alluminio Opaco y una franja en Grigio Silverstone y Rosso Fiorano. La lista de opciones suma elementos de fibra de carbono en el spoiler delantero, las aletas aerodinámicas, las tomas de aire del paragolpes, los umbrales de puerta, el tapón del depósito y los embellecedores de las llantas, además de extras como el cuentarrevoluciones en amarillo, los asientos de competición de talla grande y la suspensión delantera elevable. Parece que su propietario ha cuidado el coche con el mismo esmero que puso en configurarlo. En febrero de este año, Scuderia Monte-Carlo, el servicio oficial de Ferrari en Mónaco, le hizo una revisión completa cuando marcaba 1.119 kilómetros, y desde entonces ha recorrido menos de 20 kilómetros, entendemos que los que van del concesionario a su mansión. Cuando el propietario adquirió el coche, en 2015, un Speciale Aperta de fábrica rondaba los 300.000 euros con un equipamiento similar al de este ejemplar. Si la venta se cierra dentro del rango previsto, la revalorización se moverá entre el 233% y el 400%. Es decir, entre triplicar y quintuplicar su precio original en poco más de una década, una progresión de valor que muy pocos activos, sean coches o no, pueden igualar. Y este subidón se ha confirmado en otras ventas. Un ejemplar prácticamente gemelo, con apenas 99 kilómetros, se vendió en abril de este año en Mónaco por 1.175.000 euros, y la venta más alta jamás registrada para un Speciale Aperta ronda ya los 3 millones de dólares. Incluso la variante cupé, menos exclusiva por tratarse de un techo fijo, ha visto cómo su valor de referencia en el mercado estadounidense subía un 57% solo en el último año, hasta situarse cerca del millón de dólares en los ejemplares mejor conservados. Esta revalorización tiene una explicación en la propia política de ventas de Ferrari, que dosifica sus modelos más deseados en distintos escalones de exclusividad. En la base está la Gama, los superdeportivos de producción normal, como el Roma, el 296 o el Purosangue, que concentran el 92% de las entregas de la marca. Justo encima se sitúan las Series Especiales, con el 7% de las entregas. Se trata de evoluciones más radicales y con tiradas limitadas de los modelos de gama, entre las que se encuentra precisamente este Speciale Aperta, además de coches como el 488 Pista o el 812 Competizione. Y en la cúspide de sus modelos, con apenas el 1% de las entregas totales, están los Icona y los superdeportivos Insignia, reservados por invitación privada a los coleccionistas más importantes del planeta. Los Icona son homenajes de estética retro a la historia de la marca, como el Monza SP1 y SP2 o el Daytona SP3, mientras que los superdeportivos Insignia, el escalón más alto de todos, incluyen a auténticos hitos tecnológicos en su momento, como el LaFerrari o el más reciente F80. Para comprar un Icona o un Insignia el dinero es condición necesaria, pero ni de lejos suficiente. Acceder a esa lista depende de un historial que Ferrari vigila con lupa: cuántos coches ha comprado, si los ha conservado o vendido enseguida, cómo los han cuidado y hasta si asiste con ellos a eventos organizados por la propia marca en Maranello. Se calcula que entrar en el grupo de los cien mejores clientes del mundo exige un desembolso acumulado de entre 10 y 15 millones de euros en Ferraris. Casi nada.

articles.title: Michael Carrick demands Manchester United response after ‘pathetic’ jibes
articles.summary: With only one win so far this season, United have equalled their lowest points total in season after five matches.
articles.body:
Michael Carrick has struck a defiant tone after Manchester United equalled their worst start to a Premier League season, but a woeful 1-1 draw at Fulham left the beleaguered boss under mounting pressure.

Trailing to Lisandro Martinez’s farcical own goal, United were just moments away from a third successive defeat on another dispiriting afternoon for Carrick on Sunday.

Matheus Cunha’s deflected 89th-minute equaliser spared United from new humiliation.

But escaping with a barely deserved point against a winless side placed second-from-bottom of the Premier League was hardly cause for celebration.

With only one win so far this season, United have matched their lowest points total after five matches in the Premier League era.

Sitting in 12th place with five points, Carrick’s men equalled the mark set by Louis van Gaal’s United in 2014-15, when they went on to finish fourth.

The statistics are damning enough in their own right, but the eye test during their moribund performance at Craven Cottage provided an even more insightful look at what ails United.

Lacking a cutting edge in attack, bereft of defensive organisation and, in the words of Cunha, short of energy and drive until they fell behind, this was the kind of flawed display that has scarred so many United seasons since their last title in 2013.

Carrick was expected to build on last season’s climb to a third-place finish during his spell as interim boss.

But having hauled United from the wreckage of Ruben Amorim’s self-destructive reign, Carrick is in danger of losing his way in his first season as permanent boss.

A wretched 2-0 defeat at promoted Hull on the opening weekend set alarm bells ringing among the United faithful.

Beaten in the Manchester derby by an Erling Haaland goal that should have been disallowed last weekend, United then blew a two-goal lead at home for the first time in 50 years in a League Cup meltdown against Brighton .

Already 10 points behind leaders City, Carrick’s team were so underwhelming against Fulham that even one of the manager’s former teammates took a swipe at United.

Commenting on the match for Sky Sports, ex-United defender Gary Neville was scathing in his assessment of their performance at the start of the second half.

“I’ve watched Man United since the age of five and that’s the worst 15 minutes I’ve ever seen. Absolutely pathetic,” Neville said.

The 51-year-old added: “I’ve never seen such a lack of effort. What must Carrick be thinking?”

Carrick does not have the confrontational personality of some of his United predecessors, but he tried his best to quiet the noise as he searched for reasons for optimism.

“It’s not been ideal. It was always going to come at some point, and it’s come at the start of the season,” he said.

“On the other side of it, at Everton, a 25-yard shot, top corner for their equaliser. The City goal that’s not a goal. Today, own goal, that’s one of them things.

“It’s pretty fine margins that have flipped it. I know we can do better; we need to do better at certain things.

“But I’m not despondent because I think we’ve shown some good signs as well.”

Carrick has three weeks to stew on United’s miserable start during an extended international break.

Questions about United’s transfer policy and fitness regime are growing louder.

The 45-year-old must come up with answers before they return to action with a crucial clash against bottom-of-the-table Tottenham on October 10.

Losing to Roberto De Zerbi’s side would be a huge blow to Carrick’s hopes of turning the tide, especially with tricky trips to Atletico Madrid and Leeds looming after Tottenham visit Old Trafford.

But Carrick is putting his faith in United’s players absorbing the lessons from their painful start.

“You learn about each other, they learn about me, I learn about the individual and as a team, how we respond, what our reaction is,” he said.

“That’s part of growing as a group. You have to go through certain things to get to the end of it.”

Carrick said he had “mixed” reactions to the match but was focusing on the positives and bouncing back after this “first chapter”.

“There are parts we can do better. The way we responded to going down was really pleasing, the boys were really positive and played with good purpose,” Carrick said in a post-match interview.

“I’m convinced we’ll have a good season. We’re having a spell that feels bigger than it actually is to the outside. We’ll get back to winning football matches and we’ll be all right.”

articles.title: Mourinho entra en números rojos
articles.standfirst: Monopoly toma nota de que nunca ha ganado una Liga sumando menos de 16 puntos en las siete primeras jornadas
articles.summary: Monopoly toma nota de que nunca ha ganado una Liga sumando menos de 16 puntos en las siete primeras jornadas
articles.body: José Mourinho se despidió del Real Madrid perdiendo una final de Copa del Rey en el Santiago Bernabéu contra el Atlético de Madrid y, en el primer Derbi de su segunda etapa al frente del conjunto blanco, ha vuelto a morder el polvo en el Metropolitano. Fue una derrota dura que puso a su nuevo Real Madrid frente al espejo antes de marcharse al primer parón de selecciones de la temporada. Los blancos suman 15 puntos en las siete primeras jornadas y ya se sitúan a seis de un Barcelona que cuenta sus partidos por victorias. Monopoly ha reaccionado a este nuevo escenario y sitúa la cuota del título azulgrana en 1.22, por los 4.33 del conjunto blanco. Ese registro ha hecho entrar a Mourinho en números rojos. El técnico portugués nunca ha conseguido ganar una Liga sumando menos de 16 puntos después de las siete primeras jornadas y las apuestas deportivas también se han hecho eco de este escenario. La estadística se repite en prácticamente toda la trayectoria liguera del luso: con el Oporto sumó 17 y 19 puntos en las siete primeras jornadas de las temporadas 2002-03 y 2003-04; con el Chelsea, 17 y 21 en 2004-05 y 2005-06; en su segunda etapa en Stamford Bridge, 19 en 2014-15; con el Inter, 17 y 16 en 2008-09 y 2009-10; y con el Real Madrid, 16 en la 2011-12. No todo es negativo para el conjunto blanco si se atiende a la hemeroteca. De los nueve títulos de Liga que ha conquistado el Real Madrid a lo largo de este siglo, solamente en cuatro había sumado más de 15 puntos después de las siete primeras jornadas. El problema para Mourinho es que el Barcelona está siguiendo un ritmo intratable y ya ha abierto una brecha de seis puntos en el liderato. La evolución en las cuotas de las mejores casas de apuestas es el fiel reflejo de cómo sus opciones se han empezado a desmoronar nada más arrancar la temporada. El parón de selecciones llega, por tanto, en un momento importante para un José Mourinho que tendrá tres semanas para seguir trabajando en la mejora de un equipo que todavía no ha terminado de convencer. El objetivo, con el primer Clásico del curso en el horizonte, será evitar que la distancia con el Barcelona siga creciendo y, si acaso, recortar algo de terreno. El calendario, además, le ofrece una primera oportunidad para reaccionar: el Real Madrid recibirá al Villarreal en el Santiago Bernabéu en la próxima jornada y Monopoly cotiza su victoria a 1.27. Mourinho afrontará, por tanto, con un reto que nunca ha conseguido sacar adelante en toda su carrera: ganar una Liga después de haber sumado menos de 16 puntos en las siete primeras jornadas. Todos sus éxitos ligueros anteriores estuvieron por encima de ese registro, por lo que el portugués tendrá la difícil misión de romper por primera vez esa tendencia si quiere devolverle al Real Madrid el trono de LaLiga. Esto todavía es largo, pero no lo tendrá fácil.

articles.title: Marck Zuckerberg se enamora del pádel
articles.standfirst: El presidente de Meta, aficionado ya a otros deportes como las artes marciales mixtas, se suma como una nueva cara conocida al deporte de moda.
articles.summary: El presidente de Meta, aficionado ya a otros deportes como las artes marciales mixtas, se suma como una nueva cara conocida al deporte de moda.
articles.body: “Te voy a enseñar algo que ni te imaginas”, fue la enigmática frase con la que se abriría una conversación random, de esas que no van a ningún lado, y que precedería a la que es ya una de las fotos más impactantes de la temporada: Mark Zuckerberg jugando al pádel. Sin más recorrido que la de una imagen con una gran carga simbólica, la estampa fija de una de las personalidades más famosas del globo terráqueo asociada directamente al deporte de la pala que querían hacer llegar a MARCA Pádel sabedores del poder transformador que puede llegar a tener. Y es que según ha podido saber este periódico el magnate estadounidense ya había tenido contacto con el pádel a nivel empresarial con anterioridad, incluso había mantenido alguna conversación con los fundadores de Playtomic, pero no ha sido hasta hace muy poco que se ha dejado también atrapar por el alto poder adictivo del 20x10. Con pista de pickleball desde hace meses ya en su casa de Palo Alto, California, en el exclusivo barrio de Crescent Park, el fundador y CEO de Meta ya es jugador ocasional de pádel sumándose a una larga lista de celebridades en todo el mundo como Cristiano Ronaldo, Tom Holland, Rafa Nadal, Daddy Yankee, Ibai Llanos, Eva Longoria, Vinicius Jr, Shakira o Woody Harrelson. “No me extrañaría, sinceramente”, asegura sobre la vinculación de Zuckerberg con el pádel Marcos Del Pilar, una de las voces más autorizadas para hablar de la realidad en Estados Unidos y que lleva una década vinculado al crecimiento del deporte de la pala en suelo americano y que ha vivido en primera persona cómo algunas de las estrellas citadas se han enganchado al pádel. Con una fortuna valorada en más de 200.000 millones de euros que le sitúa en la sexta posición a nivel global según la revista Forbes, la llegada de Zuckerberg al pádel, aunque sea solo como jugador amateur, es un nuevo paso significativo para el pádel en su expansión global.
