articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Botched Finish to Sami Zayn vs. Kevin Owens Match Explained

The main event of Friday's SmackDown between Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn and Kevin Owens ended in bizarre fashion, but it sounds like neither Superstar was at fault.

In the closing moments of Zayn and Owens' championship match, CM Punk made his presence felt when he drilled Owens with the title belt. Zayn immediately went for the pin, but fans were left confused after the referee counted all the way to three but didn't call for the bell. Zayn eventually hit another Helluva Kick and pinned Owens again to end the match, but the botched ending was hard to ignore.

According to a report from Fightful Select (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), WWE sources said that Owens was never supposed to kick out after being hit with the championship belt, so the confusion arose when the referee didn't call for the bell. Zayn and Owens were forced to continue the action and create a new finish on the fly.

The match already had some shenanigans when Johnny Gargano and Candice LeRae interfered, but the shaky ending muddied the waters even further.

It's clear that WWE is building toward a three-man rivalry between Zayn, Owens and Punk, but fans need to see a cleaner operation to get fully invested in the storyline.

Contract Status Updates for Dragon Lee, Others

Dragon Lee recently impressed in his match against Intercontinental Champion Chad Gable on Monday Night Raw in Mexico City, but it sounds like his future in WWE is in question.

Wrestling Observer's Bryan Alvarez recently reported that Lee's WWE contract is nearing its expiration date. The timing of his free agency could match up with his brother, Dralistico of AEW, and there's speculation that they could look to land in the same promotion.

"Dragon Lee and Dralistico both have deals expiring fairly soon, and interestingly enough, they have trademarked the name HERMANOS LEE," Alvarez stated (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News).

Despite the uncertainty surrounding Lee's contract status, he's remained a featured member of WWE's programming. He's scheduled to compete in a Money in the Bank qualifier against Solo Sikoa and Dominik Mysterio on this week's episode of Monday Night Raw.

With WWE continuing to grow AAA as its sister promotion, Lee and Dralistico could have a prominent role if they choose to join forces. Alvarez also reported that "there are at least four Latin WWE/AEW talent whose contracts are coming due between October and February, not including Dralistico and Dragon Lee," so more Superstars could be on the move as well.

Matt Cardona Teases Injury Return Timeline

Matt Cardona recently underwent surgery to repair his torn triceps, but he's already looking ahead to his potential return to the ring.

While speaking to Katie Nolan (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News), Cardona predicted that he could be back in action early next year at one of WWE's "Big 4" premium live events.

"Yeah, the plan is to be back shorter than the surgeons say. Maybe come back to the Royal Rumble," Cardona said. "Who knows?"

Cardona went on to point out that the Royal Rumble has been pushed back from its usual January date.

"That's February this year. So, I got some time," he added.

Cardona suffered the injury last month during a match on WWE Main Event, telling Nolan he "was just too muscular that it just ripped right off my elbow."

Still, it sounds like the 41-year-old is motivated to come back with a vengeance, so he will continue to provide updates on his progress as he recovers.

articles.title: La Pizarra pone un cero al Espanyol y avisa: “Deja muy tocados al equipo y a Manolo”
articles.standfirst: El Espanyol se lleva el gran suspenso de la séptima jornada, mientras Raphinha roza la perfección y Elche y Celta consiguen el 10 antes del parón
articles.summary: El Espanyol se lleva el gran suspenso de la séptima jornada, mientras Raphinha roza la perfección y Elche y Celta consiguen el 10 antes del parón
articles.body: La séptima y última jornada antes del parón pasó por el examen de La Pizarra. Miguel Quintana, Nahuel Miranda, Adrián Blanco y Álex de Llano repartieron sus notas después de un fin de semana que dejó al Espanyol con el gran suspenso y a Elche y Celta en lo más alto. El Espanyol se llevó el gran suspenso de la jornada después de ser incapaz de controlar un partido contra diez jugadores, encajar tres goles en superioridad numérica y generar muy poco peligro más allá de los centros laterales. Miguel Quintana fue contundente: "Un cero ganado a pulso. Un 0 catedralicio. Hacía mucho que no veía a un equipo manejar tan mal la superioridad numérica". Adrián Blanco también puso el foco en las consecuencias: "Deja muy tocado al equipo y a Manolo. Va a ser un parón para que el Espanyol reflexione, porque este no es el camino". El Racing volvió a sufrir atrás y se marcha al parón como el equipo más goleado, con 21 tantos en contra. Nahuel Miranda destacó especialmente el daño de las dos últimas jornadas: "Al Racing le ha hecho mucho daño esta doble jornada con 12 goles encajados en los últimos dos partidos. Los dos primeros en Balaídos los regala". El Málaga, por su parte, pudo empatar, pero continúa sin ganar y es el equipo menos goleador, con tres tantos. Quintana avisó: "Si se pierde la magia, la química, el idilio con La Rosaleda, sí que te vas a Segunda". La Pizarra penalizó a un Real Madrid que en ningún momento transmitió sensación de peligro, con problemas en el centro del campo, un Vinicius lejos de su mejor nivel y, sobre todo, falta de intención colectiva. Nahuel resumió el momento blanco: "El Madrid está en una indefinición constante. Volvimos a ver a un Madrid muy desdibujado". Álex de Llano añadió: "15 puntos en siete jornadas es la puntuación más baja del Madrid desde la temporada 2019/2020". Adrián fue todavía más contundente: "No hay amor propio, no hay rebeldía de ese grupo". El Athletic se atascó ante la defensa del Alavés pese a terminar con 24 disparos. La gran oportunidad llegó desde el punto de penalti, pero Sivera detuvo el lanzamiento de Sancet. Es el segundo empate de los rojiblancos ante un rival que, sobre el papel, pelea por objetivos diferentes. "Es el tipo de partido que al Athletic le cuesta", señaló Quintana. El Betis continúa sufriendo defendiendo centros, tanto en jugada como a balón parado. El Deportivo encontró así el empate e incluso estuvo cerca de completar la remontada. Un problema que está siendo disimulado por el rendimiento de su portero. "Sin el nivel estratosférico de Valles, se estaría notando mucho", explicó Quintana sobre la principal asignatura pendiente del tercer clasificado, que suma 16 puntos. Ante Budimir alcanzó los 100 goles y dio un punto a Osasuna en otro partido pobre del equipo de Ramis. La Pizarra considera que el conjunto navarro necesitará mejorar durante el parón, aunque contar con el delantero facilita mucho las cosas. Nahuel lo resumió así: "Dame siempre a un futbolista como Budimir, no te esperas el remate que acaba sacando". Valencia y Real Sociedad protagonizaron el gran thriller que cerró la séptima jornada. La Real había sido muy superior, pero el encuentro se le complicó con dos apariciones de Mayol y Blázquez. Barrenetxea firmó un espectacular gol para colocar el 2-3, aunque todavía más decisiva fue la parada de Remiro ante Blázquez para conservar la victoria. Giuliano Simeone fue fundamental con un penalti forzado, una expulsión provocada y la asistencia en el gol de Jonathan David. Después de un 2026 muy pobre, firmó uno de sus mejores encuentros y resultó clave en la banda por la que se terminó decidiendo el partido. Quintana destacó su capacidad para agitar encuentros cerrados: "En un partido plano, Giuliano fuerza que pasen cosas". Adrián añadió: "En estos contextos, es un futbolista muy útil". Después de su gran encuentro ante el Málaga, Moleiro volvió a brillar con un gol y dos asistencias frente al Levante. Su sociedad con Ilias y Ayoze está siendo clave en el cambio de dinámica del Villarreal. "Moleiro está jugando muy bien de mediapunta, se le está viendo muy cómodo. Da gusto verle jugando por dentro", destacó Adrián. La actuación de Raphinha volvió a dejar impresionada a La Pizarra. Sus movimientos, su capacidad para definir después de ir al sprint y sus números le colocan como uno de los grandes protagonistas del inicio liguero. Quintana no escatimó elogios: "Es una exageración, es excepcional, rompe cualquier lógica: 12 goles en siete partidos". El Elche de Martín Anselmi recibió la máxima nota después de saber jugar con y sin balón incluso en inferioridad. Quintana señaló la importancia que puede adquirir esta victoria con el paso del tiempo: "Es un espaldarazo tremendo para un proyecto que está conviviendo con demasiados errores individuales no forzados que podían llevarlo al desastre". De Llano añadió: "Había gente que dudaba de Fer Niño". El otro sobresaliente fue para el Celta, que goleó al Racing gracias, entre otras cosas, a su presión en los reinicios y a las actuaciones de Ilaix Moriba y Miguel Román. Después del desastre en Nicosia, el triunfo permite afrontar el parón con otro ánimo. "Veremos si es un punto de inflexión en la temporada", apuntó Quintana. Adrián aseguró que "es una victoria que debe dar un respiro y tranquilidad al Celta", mientras que De Llano concluyó: "Es el típico partido que puede servir para cambiar dinámicas".

articles.title: Luke Littler withdraws from Players Championship events after hopes of PDC title sweep dashed
articles.summary: Luke Littler has withdrawn from two Players Championship events in the Netherlands after his hopes of completing a clean sweep of PDC major titles this season ended in Amsterdam; the world No 1 had already threatened to boycott Dutch events after crowd abuse
articles.body:
World No 1 Littler was dumped out of the World Series of Darts Finals at the quarter-final stage by a 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton on Sunday, ending his run of winning the first six premier events of the season.

The 19-year-old had been scheduled to feature at Players Championship 29 and 30 in Den Bosch, Netherlands, on Tuesday and Wednesday but has pulled out of both events, a decision which effectively ends his chances of qualifying for November's finals in Minehead.

'The Nuke' sits 125th on the Order of Merit in the Players Championship circuit, £16,750 adrift of the final qualification spot on offer to the top 64 players.

Littler's decision follows the teenager threatening to boycott tournaments in the Netherlands after he was subjected to boos and whistles during the World Series of Darts Finals.

The Amsterdam crowd jeered the two-time world champion throughout his first-round match against home favourite Danny Noppert, with Littler saying he would take the same stance with the Netherlands as he does with Germany after being subjected to fan abuse there.

"With the Germans, I haven't been for a long time. We will have to see in Dortmund whether it changes or stays the same," he told Online Darts. "If the Dutch stay like this, then I'm not going to do any Euro Tours over there.

"There's just no point in me travelling, wasting my time while I'm getting booed. I just want to play my darts, obviously sign autographs.

"The past two nights, I've done nothing. I've just walked off stage without thanking anybody. There's no point thanking everyone when they are booing me."

articles.title: Early Predictions for Roman Reigns, CM Punk and WWE WrestleMania 43 Match Card
articles.summary: CM Punk and Roman Reigns headlined WrestleMania 42 in Las Vegas, delivering not only one of the best matches of 2026 but one of the greatest main events in the long and illustrious history of the Showcase of the Immortals.
articles.body:
CM Punk and Roman Reigns headlined WrestleMania 42 in Las Vegas, delivering not only one of the best matches of 2026 but one of the greatest main events in the long and illustrious history of the Showcase of the Immortals.

While they are unlikely to run it back again in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia in 2027, they will still be prominently featured on the lineup, likely in marquee roles.

What awaits those two and what are other matches fans might expect from the next edition of the Granddaddy of Them All?

World Heavyweight Championship Match: Oba Femi vs. Roman Reigns (c)

Undisputed WWE Championship Match: CM Punk vs. Cody Rhodes

Women's World Championship Match: Stephanie Vaquer vs. Becky Lynch

WWE Women's Championship Match: Rhea Ripley vs. Charlotte Flair

Intercontinental Championship Ladder Match: Je'Von Evans vs. Chad Gable vs. Ethan Page vs. Dominik Mysterio vs. JD McDonagh vs. Big Cass

United States Championship Match: Trick Williams vs. Carmelo Hayes

Women's Tag Team Championship Match : Tatum Paxley and Alexa Bliss vs. The Bella Twins vs. Fatal Influence

Penta, Rey Fenix, and Seth Rollins vs. The Usos and Jacob Fatu

Bi-Annual "We Don't Know What Else to Do With Them So Here You Go Again" Match: Kevin Owens vs. Sami Zayn

As is typically the case, the undercard is a total crapshoot. While the main event scene has some nods to what fans can expect at the event, the undercard is unlikely to be even considered until much closer to the show than we currently are.

There will inevitably be a star or two left off the card entirely, while the lineup is good for at least one "throw as many guys as we can in one match so we can get everyone on the show" championship ladder match.

The most obvious clash is Reigns defending the World Heavyweight Championship against Femi while Punk vs. Rhodes in a rematch of their one-off SummerSlam match feels like the right direction for the loaded SmackDown main event scene.

Beyond those two matches, everything else is a total guesstimate at this point in time as WWE's creative team has probably not even begun to think about contests outside of the top of the card.

Regardless of whether one believes him to be the best wrestler in the world or not, Reigns is the measuring stick in WWE. He is the guy every prospective main event star must test themselves against if they want to even think about taking his spot.

After a monumental first year on the main roster in which he bested "The Beast" Brock Lesnar in two out of three battles, won the King of the Ring, and is the overwhelming favorite to win the Royal Rumble, Femi is the next guy to step up to The OTC and try him on the biggest stage in professional wrestling.

A marquee match-up between the hottest young star on the roster and the guy who holds the record for most WrestleMania main events ever, it is of WrestleMania-worthy magnitude and should be the coronation of the next star to carry the company for the next decade-plus.

This, however, would not be the time for WWE to get cute, overthink the outcome, or try to push the inevitable off for another year.

Unlike when Cody Rhodes had to wait an additional 365 days to really earn that Undisputed WWE Championship victory at WrestleMania 40, Femi must defeat Reigns and win the title in Riyadh, thus capitalizing on his immense popularity.

Anything else would be a monumental creative failure, especially after the lengths Lesnar went to establish Femi as the future of the industry.

At SummerSlam, CM Punk and Cody Rhodes squared off in a battle of babyfaces that split the crowd in Minneapolis and ultimately was overshadowed by the return of Randy Orton late in the bout.

The screwy finish, which saw The Viper drop Rhodes with an RKO to set up Punk's successful retention, was fine and propelled one storyline forward, but it failed to answer whether The Best in the World or The American Nightmare was truly the better man.

Conveniently enough, Rhodes and Punk have been kept apart on TV ever since.

Even during his sit-down interview with Michael Cole on the September 18 episode of SmackDown, when naming the men who celebrated in the ring with him after his greatest victory at WrestleMania 40, Rhodes failed to name Punk.

Perhaps it is because the former WWE champion never officially turned on him or did anything truly awful to QB1. Or, perhaps, it was cleverly designed so as not to spoil a second showdown between the two in Riyadh.

Whatever the case, a WrestleMania-sized match-up between the two biggest stars on Friday nights feels like the appropriate direction, if for no other reason than the fact that it is still a relatively fresh match-up with unsettled issues at the forefront.

articles.title: El once ideal de septiembre de La Pizarra: Raphinha repite, Lamine entra y Rodri manda
articles.standfirst: Álvaro Valles se hace con la portería de un equipo en el que también aparecen Cubarsí, Grimaldo, Moleiro o Camello
articles.summary: Álvaro Valles se hace con la portería de un equipo en el que también aparecen Cubarsí, Grimaldo, Moleiro o Camello
articles.body: La Pizarra ya tiene su once ideal del mes de septiembre. Después del debate que provocó la elección de agosto, Miguel Quintana, Adrián Blanco, Nahuel Miranda y Álex de Llano volvieron a poner sobre la mesa los nombres propios que más han destacado durante el último mes. El resultado es un 4-4-2 con representación de varios equipos y con Raphinha como único futbolista que repite. No hubo demasiada discusión bajo palos. Álvaro Valles fue el elegido después de cerrar septiembre con 21 paradas y únicamente tres goles encajados. "Para mí está mejor ahora", apuntó Quintana al comparar su versión actual en el Betis con aquella gran primera vuelta que protagonizó con Las Palmas. Alfonso Herrero y David Soria fueron otros de los nombres mencionados, pero ninguno consiguió discutir realmente el puesto a Valles. "Es el mejor portero en lo que va de Liga, está salvando al Betis", añadió Nahuel. En el lateral derecho aparece Juan Iglesias, elegido por delante de alternativas como Andrei Ratiu. El defensa cerró el mes con un 61% de duelos ganados, 11 despejes y 10 recuperaciones, además de un gol decisivo. "El nivel que está dando con el Sevilla me está encantando, es muy competitivo", explicó Adrián. La pareja de centrales la forman Pau Cubarsí y Natan. El azulgrana sobresalió, entre otros registros, con un 78% de duelos aéreos ganados. "Es una barbaridad el dato", destacó Quintana sobre un central que considera fundamental para explicar el pleno del Barça durante septiembre. "Ha arrancado como un tiro", añadió Nahuel. Natan, por su parte, acumuló 31 despejes, 11,5 duelos ganados por partido y cinco remates bloqueados. "Su rendimiento, junto al de Valles, fue una de las claves del buen mes del Betis", señaló Quintana. Cuti Romero y Joel Lago aparecieron también en la conversación como alternativas para el centro de la defensa. El lateral izquierdo es para Alejandro Grimaldo, autor de dos goles y una asistencia, además de crear dos ocasiones claras. Su inicio de mes dejó alguna duda, pero su rendimiento fue creciendo con el paso de los partidos. Para Adrián, "el partido del rojiblanco ante la Real Sociedad ha marcado un punto de inflexión". Adrià Pedrosa fue otro de los nombres que entró en la discusión. En la medular aparece Rodri Hernández. Su actuación ante el Sevilla terminó por convencer a todos. "El partido que hace ante el Sevilla es partido del mejor mediocentro del mundo", afirmó Adrián Blanco. Además de su influencia con balón, destacaron su rendimiento defensivo y su capacidad para imponerse en los duelos. A su lado está Fofana, una de las grandes apariciones del Sevilla. Terminó septiembre con un gol y 29 recuperaciones, además de promediar 21 conducciones por encuentro. "Tiene cosas, fundamentos top, es un futbolista que, por economía, el Sevilla no se hubiera podido permitir", señalaron durante el análisis de un centrocampista que ha entrado con fuerza". En la derecha no hubo sitio para demasiadas dudas: Lamine Yamal. Después de quedarse fuera del once de agosto, el azulgrana entra en septiembre gracias a cinco goles, cuatro asistencias y 16 regates completados. El pequeño "asterisco" del equipo aparece en la izquierda. El elegido es Alberto Moleiro, aunque sus mejores actuaciones llegaron con mayor libertad por dentro. Sus dos goles, dos asistencias y 12 ocasiones creadas terminaron inclinando la balanza: "Moleiro ha estado excepcional, sobre todo en los últimos dos partidos". La enorme competencia en la delantera dejó fuera nombres como Roberto Fernández, Fer Niño, Jonathan David, Mbappé o Lucas Boyé, pero La Pizarra se quedó finalmente con Sergio Camello y Raphinha. Camello marcó cuatro goles y dio una asistencia, con tres de sus tantos cambiando la dinámica del marcador. Pero su elección no se explica únicamente por las cifras. "Está muy fino, tiene confianza para atreverse a hacer cosas, lo está bordando", destacó Adrián. Su rendimiento incluso abrió el debate sobre una posible llamada de la selección en próximas convocatorias. Y el once se cierra con el único superviviente del equipo de agosto: Raphinha. El brasileño terminó septiembre con siete goles y continúa disparado en este inicio de temporada. "Evidentemente, el MVP de lo que va de Liga", sentenció Quintana. "Está súper acertado, pero son definiciones que son acciones casi de seguridad", explicaron en La Pizarra sobre un jugador cuyo nivel de confianza ha crecido después de su cambio de posición. El encargado de dirigir este once es Hansi Flick. La Pizarra había premiado a Quique Sánchez Flores en agosto, pero esta vez el pleno del Barcelona terminó con cualquier debate. "Segundo mes consecutivo, su equipo jugando como los ángeles. Impecable", resumió Quintana.

articles.title: Derwin James: We have to tell the truth, we look like trash
articles.summary: The Chargers are 0-2 after losses to the Cardinals and Raiders.
articles.body:
Any hopes that the Chargers' loss to the Cardinals was just a Week 1 aberration were dashed at SoFi Stadium on Sunday.

The Raiders scored the final 16 points of the game to take a 26-14 win over their division rivals and move to 2-0 on the season. The Chargers are 0-2 after two games many pegged as easy wins for the team heading into the season.

Both sides of the ball have contributed to both of the losses and safety Derwin James said the first step to turning things around is being honest about just how bad the first two weeks have gone.

"We got to look each other in the eye, man, and just tell the truth and just get better," James said in the locker room. "Because right now that s—t just looks trash. . . . I'm angry, but being angry don't fix anything. Being angry don't fix the problem that we have. We have to get it fixed. I feel like we're a couple of plays away. It ain't like we're getting blown out. But we have to win these games, there's no reason we're going out there playing like that."

The Cardinals also beat the Chargers 26-14 and it's difficult to make the argument that it's just a couple of plays deciding things when you're losing by double digits at home. Whatever the case, the Chargers don't have much time to make the necessary connections. They are in Buffalo and Seattle the next two weeks and losses in those games will have them looking at a very long and very disappointing season in Southern California.

articles.title: ‘I had no choice’: MMA fighter Varun Sanyal breaks silence after weight-cut blackout, calls himself ‘foolish’
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: India’s MMA fighter Varun Sanyal has broken his silence after being forced to withdraw from the Asian Games following a blackout during a s.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s MMA fighter Varun Sanyal has broken his silence after being forced to withdraw from the Asian Games following a blackout during a sauna session, admitting that his attempt to cut weight on his own was “quite foolish” but saying he felt he had no choice.Sanyal, who was due to compete in the men’s traditional 77kg event, passed out on Sunday while trying to make weight at his cruise-ship accommodation. He was subsequently declared medically unfit and could not compete.“I came here on two weeks' notice, I found out relatively late. I obviously had a bunch of accommodation issues, and then I was all by myself on a weight cut. In retrospect, that was quite foolish of me to do,” Sanyal told PTI.“I had no choice but to do it by myself. That's a question, to be honest, I would like the public to ask, why was I alone? But, you know, things happen, life goes on. I don't want to sit here and feel sorry for myself.”‘I am disappointed, but I’m more proud’Sanyal, 27, was included in India’s Asian Games squad on September 2 after a late selection process. The MMA team travelled to Aichi-Nagoya without support staff, leaving Sanyal to manage his weight cut alone.“Yeah, absolutely, I am disappointed. I had wanted to participate and show off my skills. I have big aspirations for myself in this sport, and I have backed myself to do well. But yeah, I have moved on,” he said.“I think rather than focusing on what could happen, we focus on what did. And despite all the challenges that the federation has faced over the last year, we came out with a medal, it is huge. So, yeah, rather than being disappointed, I'm more proud of such a good result.”Suchika Tariyal won India’s first medal in MMA at the Games after losing in the semifinals of the women’s traditional 60kg event.‘On two weeks’ notice, I found out’Sanyal said he had qualified for the Asian Games in January but eventually shifted his attention towards his professional career amid uncertainty over the selection process.“I qualified for Asian Games back in January. But there was a lot of uncertainty surrounding the qualification process. So, I decided to shift focus to my professional career. And I didn't want the slot to go empty. There was another athlete who had put his hands up and he qualified, or he went for the qualifications in Uzbekistan back in May,” he said.“However, he didn't rank high enough in Asia. I was fourth ranked in Asia. I was getting ready for a professional fight in the cage. And then, on two weeks' notice, I found out that my name was announced (for Asian Games). So, here I am.”Sanyal’s blackout came after he had earlier spoken about the logistical problems at the Games, including athletes having to wait eight to 10 hours without food before getting their rooms.MMA Sports Federation of India president Nikhil Kunder said Sanyal was found unconscious by a Nepalese athlete, who woke him and alerted officials.“Fortunately, he was found in that state by an athlete from Nepal who woke him up. Varun was able to call me and we took him to hospital,” Kunder had told PTI.The Indian Olympic Association said Sanyal suffered “generalised cramps and body ache” while in the sauna. articles.title: Rangers take 'amazing feeling' into international break - Naderi
articles.summary: Rangers will carry the "awesome" feeling of back-to-back derby victories through the international break, says Parkhead hero Ryan Naderi.  The German striker...
articles.body:
Rangers will carry the "awesome" feeling of back-to-back derby victories through the international break, says Parkhead hero Ryan Naderi.

The German striker, 23, scored the only goal of the game on Sunday as Rangers moved to within two points of their rivals at the top of the Scottish Premiership, having knocked Celtic out of the League Cup a week earlier.

His all-round game was impressive as he led Rangers' press, ran channels and linked play, in addition to his tidy first-time finish.

"It's awesome, to be honest, to win two times against Celtic, and then go into a break is an amazing feeling," Naderi said.

"You will carry this throughout the whole days and weeks off.

"We have to still understand that we have a whole season in front of us still.

"So we should just keep this up, not fly too high, just stay focused and keep going as we are, stay together as a team, even in bad times and good times, it's just important to always stick together as a team and go forward.

"Really big [win] honestly, really big."

Naderi, who shook off an ankle injury to start on Sunday, says the team spirit in the Rangers dressing room is now obvious after a tricky start to the campaign.

"With the win at home we wanted to go there and show that we can do it away as well," he said.

"Amazing fight from the whole team, good spirit from the whole game and just so happy to win there.

"I think you see this togetherness, by the goals we concede, not many. We play a lot of games to zero.

"That means that we just are very compact, we work together, look at each other, where the person next to you stands, and when you're so stable defensively, you will always have chances to score and then you win games."

articles.title: Chris Finch Addresses How LaMelo Ball Will Change Timberwolves’ Identity
articles.summary: Will the Minnesota Timberwolves play faster?
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves are expected to take on a new identity this upcoming season as they've revamped their starting lineup to better suit how Anthony Edwards plays.

Gone are Julius Randle and Naz Reid, who had their respective strengths on the offensive end, with Randle playing bully ball while showing his playmaking skills, and Reid acting as a stretch four while being able to put the ball on the floor a bit.

In are LaMelo Ball and Jonathan Kuminga , who bring a different set of skills to the table. LaMelo plays fast and loose with the ball, finding creative ways to get his shot off and get the ball to his teammates. Kuminga plays a straightforward game, and he drives to the basket.

Speaking to the Minnesota Post , Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch addressed how the team might play with its new-look roster.

"To be determined. As I sit here now, I want to see how it plays out. Your identity is driven by your best players, for sure, and we still have them. I can see a lot of our offensive identity still flowing through Ant. It is just that I think we have a chance to play faster, be a better passing team, maybe people benefit from off-ball movement more. With Rudy, a lot of different things (can happen), so I can see everything kind of get a little polished, if you will. But ultimately a lot of our identity is still going to flow through Anthony a lot," he said.

Anthony Edwards remains the best player on the team and one of the best scorers in the league, finishing third in scoring last season.

Minnesota finished 13th in the league in offense last season, and they've consistently been a top ten defense under Finch.

If they don't, something has gone wrong.

Between LaMelo, Edwards, Jaden McDaniels, and Kuminga, this is a team with great athleticism and ability to get to the rim. They should be pushing the ball upcourt, taking advantage of transition opportunities with their speed and strength.

Gobert is the weak link offensively, but his screen setting should continue to open things up, and his rebounding will end a lot of defensive possessions, which should allow them to immediately push the pace and capitalize on defenses that are not set.

The ball has a chance to move a lot more with LaMelo being the first true top-tier point guard that Edwards has ever played with and McDaniels making a leap. The offense can still flow through Edwards, but buckets should come much easier for him in the new starting lineup.

articles.title: Jean-Mattéo Bahoya reacts to Elland Road debut and squad welcome
articles.summary: It might only have been the briefest of Elland Road cameos but Jean-Mattéo Bahoya began to realise a childhood dream with his Leeds United debut against Crys...
articles.body:
It might only have been the briefest of Elland Road cameos but Jean-Mattéo Bahoya began to realise a childhood dream with his Leeds United debut against Crystal Palace .

The Frenchman got the call from the bench with a minute of regulation time remaining, but with the ball not going out of play for an extended period of time he was made to wait until the 91st minute to make his entrance.

Between coming on and the 93rd-minute full-time whistle Bahoya managed at least to contribute something. He twice applied pressure to Palace to help force a turnover, ran onto Anton Stach 's ball down the line and won a free-kick in an attacking position that led to a yellow card for Jefferson Lerma . When the set-piece was half cleared, Bahoya picked up the loose ball, beat a man and drew two others before finding Stach - just as the final whistle went.

As cameos go it was brief, but the deadline-day signing was delighted to get his first minutes at a sold-out Elland Road.

"There was a lot of emotion," he said. "I was proud because when I was young, it was one of my dreams to play in the Premier League. So now I'm happy to play in this stadium at home, with this atmosphere. A really good start. Not the best for the team because we had only one point, but it was a good point to keep going."

At 21 years of age Bahoya is one of the most junior members of Daniel Farke's senior squad. He signed for the club on the last day of the summer transfer window in a deal that was worked on right up until the deadline. But in the 20 days that have followed, he has found the transition to English football straightforward thanks to the presence of former Frankfurt team-mate Michael Zetterer and the way the squad have welcomed him.

"It was easy because I know Zetterer, he's a new player also, but he helped me a lot, and the team was really good with me. A lot of guys helped me outside the pitch and on the training pitch. So no, it was easy for me to join this club."

articles.title: The 76ers Could Have Interest in Two Hornets Players, If Things Don’t Work Out With Their New Additions
articles.summary: The 76ers want two Hornets players. Not stars, not franchise cornerstones — but two rotation pieces that Philadelphia has specifically identified as fits for...
articles.body:
The 76ers want two Hornets players. Not stars, not franchise cornerstones — but two rotation pieces that Philadelphia has specifically identified as fits for what they are building around Tyrese Maxey , Jaylen Brown and LeBron James .

Ryan Kalkbrenner and Dennis Schroder are the names, and the conversation around both of them tells you something interesting about where Charlotte stands heading into the season. Not every trade has to be a blockbuster. Sometimes the small ones reveal the most.

Philadelphia let Andre Drummond walk without a fight this summer and signed Ariel Hukporti to compete for the primary backup center role behind Joel Embiid . The Sixers also dumped Johni Broome in a trade to create space. If Hukporti and Adem Bona do not work out — and there is no guarantee they will — Kalkbrenner becomes exactly the kind of affordable, size-and-shot-blocking option a front office calls about quietly in November.

At $2.4 million for the season, Kalkbrenner is one of the most affordable big men in the league relative to what he provides. He stands 7-foot-1, averaged 1.5 blocks per game last season, shot 75.3% from the field, and brought 5.5 rebounds per game in limited minutes. He is not a stretch five and will not create offense, but as a rim-protecting backup who costs nothing and does not demand the ball, he fits the Sixers' template perfectly.

From Charlotte's side, the question is whether parting with him makes sense. Hannes Steinbach is the long-term frontcourt answer, but he is 19 years old and still finding his footing at the professional level. The Hornets also don't have much frontcourt depth behind starters Moussa Diabate , Naz Reid and Steinbach. Kalkbrenner is the only other true center with rim-protection ability on the roster. Trading him leaves a gap that nobody else currently fills.

The $2.4 million price tag also means he essentially costs nothing to keep — making the bar to trade him higher than the number suggests.

If Philadelphia offers Jabari Walker — a 23-year-old forward with legitimate two-way upside — or Justin Edwards for Kalkbrenner, the conversation changes. Charlotte gets a young piece with real developmental ceiling. Philly gets their backup center. Both teams solve a specific problem without overpaying. That version of the deal is worth picking up the phone for.

Schroder is the more complicated conversation. Philadelphia wants insurance behind Maxey in case Labaron Philon Jr . is not ready for a playoff run — and Schroder, with 13 NBA seasons and playoff experience across multiple franchises, fits that profile. His 2025 postseason run with Detroit — 12.5 points, 49.1% from the field, 47.6% from three, 3.7 assists to 1.2 turnovers per game — is the version of him that makes contenders take notice.

But Charlotte signed Schroder specifically to solve their own backup point guard problem. When Coby White sits, Schroder runs the offense. That role exists because the Summer League losses to New Orleans painfully exposed what Charlotte looks like without a real ball-handler managing the second unit.

Trading him means going back to Christian Anderson — a rookie still finding his professional footing — as the primary backup. Schroder's $14.8 million salary also makes the trade math complicated for Philadelphia, which would almost certainly need to move Anfernee Simons and additional pieces to make it work.

Unless Philadelphia sends back a piece that directly addresses Charlotte's needs, the Schroder trade does not make sense for this roster right now. He is not just a veteran contract. He is a functional part of a rotation that Charlotte has not yet fully tested.

The Last Word On The 76ers Want Two Hornets Players

The 76ers' potential interest in two Hornets players is not the most dramatic trade story of the offseason — but it is a useful reminder that Charlotte has assets other teams value, even beyond the obvious names. Kalkbrenner is a bargain that almost any team would take.

Schroder is a veteran who has proven he can perform in postseason situations. Both have real market value. Whether Jeff Peterson picks up the phone depends on what comes back — and right now, the bar needs to be higher than what Philadelphia has publicly floated. Charlotte is not a parts depot. They are building something. Every trade has to make that something better, not just lighter.

Do you think Charlotte should trade Kalkbrenner, Schroder, both, or neither? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Greg Van Roten was ready when Patriots needed him most
articles.summary: Patriots veteran guard Greg Van Roten was ready to step up when Mike Onwenu went down against the Steelers.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass — The worst-case scenario became a reality for the New England Patriots on Sunday when starting right guard Mike Onwenu went down with an injury in the first quarter.

But, fortunately for New England, Greg Van Roten was ready for that exact type of moment, stepping in when his team needed him most.

"I mean, you're just trying to stay ready in case something happens and you got to go in. And Mike went down, and I don't know if it's going to be for one play or for the rest of the game," Van Roten said in a 1-on-1 conversation with Patriots Wire. "So you're really just trying to take it one play at a time. And if you have a good play, you want to build on that. If you have a bad play, you want to kind of push it aside, find out why it went wrong, correct it, and move on. So for me, I knew it wasn't my best game, but we won, and that's what matters at the end of the day. And there's a lot to improve on personally and as a unit."

Van Roten slotted in next to Morgan Moses, which also helped as the two had a lot of familiarity playing with one another.

"So Morgan and I actually played next to each other on the Jets in 2021," he explained. "So we've banked a lot of experience together. So I have familiarity with him, and he's obviously a really great tackle. So it's very easy to go out there. I don't have to worry about him. He doesn't have to worry about me. And we've both played a lot of football, so it's really just, it's good to be out there with an experienced group like that."

And he also knows Josh McDaniels' system, having played for him in Las Vegas during the 2023 season, serving as the team's starting right guard.

"In the beginning, it's a lot of mental stuff and just kind of catching up on the playbook. But I've been in the system, so I have familiarity with that," Van Roten said. "And that was kind of one of the reasons that they wanted me was because I knew the system, I can play multiple positions. So the beginning is mental, and then it's just physically trying to get yourself into football shape, which is really hard to do unless you're playing football. So this is my first couple quarters and we'll see how many more they need me for."

Onwenu was immediately ruled out of the game with an ankle injury and shortly after the final whistle blew, it was reported that he suffered a broken ankle, sidelining him longterm. So, that means the team will likely turn to Van Roten to fill that void for the foreseeable future.

"As long as they need me and want me. I love to play, and I want to keep playing," Van Roten said. "So we'll see what's up with Mike and kind of go from there."

articles.title: Detroit Tigers to Announce New Comerica Park Name
articles.summary: The Tigers and Fifth Third Bank will announce a new name for Comerica Park, with the rebranding expected to begin in 2027.
articles.body:
Comerica Park is entering its final season under the only name it has ever carried.

The Detroit Tigers and Fifth Third Bank are expected to announce a new name for the downtown ballpark Monday, according Brad Galli . The change is expected to take effect for the 2027 season.

The specific name was not included in the initial report. Fifth Third Park, Fifth Third Field and other variations may appear obvious, but none should be treated as official until the Tigers and bank complete their announcement.

Comerica Park opened in 2000 as the replacement for Tiger Stadium. The ballpark has carried Comerica's name throughout its 27-season history, making this more than a routine signage change for a generation of Tigers fans.

Fifth Third Acquisition Forces a Familiar Name Aside

The expected rebranding follows Fifth Third Bancorp's acquisition of Comerica in a $10.9 billion all-stock transaction. The deal, announced in October 2025 , combined two major regional banks and created one of the country's largest banking institutions.

Fifth Third and Comerica completed their merger in February. The companies are now operating as one organization, with Fifth Third gradually replacing the Comerica brand across the combined business.

That made a ballpark name change likely even though Comerica had extended its naming-rights agreement with the Tigers through 2034. The corporate identity behind the agreement changed, and the stadium branding is now following it.

The building itself is not changing hands. The Detroit-Wayne County Stadium Authority owns the ballpark, while the Tigers remain its primary tenant. This is a naming-rights and branding change, not a relocation, ownership transfer or plan for a new stadium.

The Name Changes, but the Tigers' Home Does Not

Comerica Park has hosted Tigers baseball since its first game in April 2000 . It has also staged the 2005 MLB All-Star Game, postseason runs, concerts, hockey games and several rounds of renovations.

The 2026 season will now represent the final chapter for the Comerica Park name. It already carries historical weight because Justin Verlander is retiring after the season , giving fans two familiar pieces of Tigers identity to say goodbye to.

Detroit is also evaluating players who could shape the club's next era while continuing to manage roster changes such as Casey Mize's move to the injured list . The new ballpark name will arrive as that transition moves into 2027.

Fans may resist the new branding at first. Stadium names become geographical shorthand, especially after nearly three decades. The official name will change, but Detroiters will decide how quickly they stop calling the place Comerica Park.

Randal Kolo Muani is proud of the mindset Juventus showed as they beat Atalanta 2-0 in Serie A this weekend, and he hopes that mentality continues.

Juventus performed well in their midweek match against NEC in the Europa League , but their main challenge is the Scudetto, and this season is one in which they need to perform consistently.

The men at the Allianz Stadium have so far been among the top teams in the league, but they need to maintain their good form, and that means winning more matches.

Against Atalanta , Juventus were facing one of the trickiest teams in the division, and they knew it would not be an easy match. It was therefore a performance they could be proud of, particularly after returning to winning ways in the league.

La Dea remain a top team despite their start to the season, and they threatened to cause problems during the game. However, Juventus rose to the occasion and secured an important victory.

The result also showed that Juventus can respond when faced with a difficult challenge. They had to remain focused throughout the match, and their performance ultimately allowed them to take all three points.

(Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

It is still a long season, and only a few games have been played by all the teams. However, the men in black and white will be determined to finish the campaign strongly, and their display against Atalanta provided another positive sign.

Kolo Muani was pleased with the mentality shown by his teammates and believes they must continue in the same manner. Speaking about the victory, Tuttomercatoweb quoted him as saying:

"This is the right mentality, we wanted to win and we did it. We're very happy with the three points. It was a great evening, the crowd was incredible. We need to keep going like this."

Kolo Muani's comments reflect the importance Juventus places on maintaining their current approach. With the league campaign still in its early stages, continuing to produce performances that lead to victories will be important if they want to remain among the leading teams.

articles.body:
The Ravens held an 11-point lead over the Saints in the first half on Sunday and they were up by eight points heading into the fourth quarter, but two Saints touchdowns made New Orleans 24-17 winners in Baltimore when the final whistle sounded.

It was a familiar place for the Ravens to find themselves. It was the 15th time the team has lost a game in which it held a double-digit lead since the start of the 2019 season, but the first 14 of those came with John Harbaugh as their head coach. This was the first with Jesse Minter and cornerback Marlon Humphrey said after the game that the Ravens have to make sure this does not remain part of their DNA.

"The consensus amongst the team is like, everyone is kind of tired of doing what we just did ," Humphrey said, via the team's website. "I think it is a lot of older guys — a lot of guys that it just feels like it is time. Hopefully we will make this a hiccup and not [let] this be a bridge that is final and cannot be repaired."

Tight end Mark Andrews said that "there is not one similarity I can feel" to previous seasons and the onus will be on him, Humphrey and other team leaders to make sure that the team isn't deploying the same old formula in new packaging.

articles.title: Jim Nantz, J.J. Watt share awkward moment in second week together
articles.summary: Jim Nantz isn't always listening when J.J. Watt talks.
articles.body:
Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt called the Week 2 matchup between the New England Patriots and Pittsburgh Steelers . It was the duo's second regular season game together following Tony Romo 's offseason arrest. Romo's future with CBS remains up in the air while the network watches how things progress between Nantz and Watt.

If Sunday's game was an indication, they still have some work to do. During the first quarter Watt shared a story about a meeting they had with Steelers' coach Mike McCarthy . After the Week 1 win he was surprised with a game ball from Aaron Rodgers in the locker room. The story obviously made an impression on both Nantz and Watt.

I'm not sure Jim Nantz was paying attention when JJ Watt was talking here 😂 pic.twitter.com/RWzzjkTXeS — Nicholas Callas (@CALLAS_33) September 20, 2026

I'm not sure Jim Nantz was paying attention when JJ Watt was talking here 😂 pic.twitter.com/RWzzjkTXeS

Nicholas Callas (@CALLAS_33) September 20, 2026

"He talked to us about how emotional he got after that first win when getting the game ball from Aaron Rodgers and just how special it was," Watt told the audience.

Nantz, without missing a beat added, "He got the game ball too, in the locker room from Aaron Rodgers after. It was quite a moment. It was captured."

So maybe he did miss a beat. Specifically the beat where Watt just told the same story. This kind of thing does happen when someone gets distracted, but to hear such a clear example of someone not listening in the booth is shocking.

Still, these two have only been together a few weeks at this point. The rest of the call was perfectly fine and other than this very clear hiccup, it's been a good start to the season for Watt . There's no reason this pairing won't work the entire season, but Nantz should probably make an effort to hear his partner in the near future.

articles.title: ‘1000% awesome’ – Fans erupt as Sophie Cunningham used as bizarre ‘distraction’ vs Troy Trojans
articles.summary: The Missouri Tigers won against the Troy Trojans 27-17 in NCAA Football to keep their unbeaten streak, and they can perhaps thank…Sophie Cunningham for it? M...
articles.body:
The Missouri Tigers won against the Troy Trojans 27-17 in NCAA Football to keep their unbeaten streak, and they can perhaps thank… Sophie Cunningham for it?

Missouri is Sophie Cunningham's alma mater, having a great career with the Missouri Tigers' basketball team before playing for the Indiana Fever .

As it turns out, Cunningham is helping her alma mater years after leaving, as the fans erupted at the player being used as a bizarre distraction tactic in the Tigers' 27-17 win against the Trojans.

Missouri Tigers' Sophie Cunningham distraction tactic

Late in the fourth quarter, when the Trojans made it an unexpectedly tricky game for the Tigers, their kicker Ethan Head lined up a 54-yard field-goal attempt.

Just behind it was the jumbotron, where the Tigers displayed a huge image of Sophie Cunningham pointing directly at the goal.

Had Head succeeded, this would have become a one-score game, but the bizarre distraction tactic worked. Head missed, and the Tigers closed out a nervy game.

The fans erupted in equal parts hilarity and bewilderment at what the Tigers pulled off.

"This is 1000% awesome and a high-five to the person who thought of that," said one fan, as another agreed, "This is going to be epic. Massive trolling incoming."

A third said they wanted to "build the statue" for Sophie Cunningham as she keeps helping her alma mater years after moving on to professional basketball.

"This needs to become a trend," joked another, as a fifth said, "That lady would distract me, no problem!" Another said, "When I saw this I was laughing so hard. I love it."

One didn't find it as funny. They were probably a Troy Trojans fan! They wrote, "That would actually help them kick it through. Just aim it at her face."

"One can't blame them. Sophie Cunningham distracts me every time I see her," one fan jokingly sympathized with the Trojans' kicker.

For her part, Cunningham dropped a dud in her next game as Indiana Fever lost to Washington Mystics . Cunningham played just seven minutes and missed both of her only 3PT attempts to finish with zero points.

The good day's work was done earlier for her alma mater, it seems!

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes sums up Chiefs’ overtime escape against Colts
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes threw for 382 yards and three touchdowns before Harrison Butker delivered the final points in Kansas City’s 33-30 overtime victory.
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes needed only seven words to describe how the Kansas City Chiefs survived Sunday night.

"We fought until the very end," Mahomes said during his postgame press conference .

It was the perfect summary of a 33-30 overtime victory over the Indianapolis Colts that required every available second.

Harrison Butker kicked a 40-yard field goal as overtime expired, finally ending a game in which Indianapolis repeatedly answered Kansas City . Butker had already connected from 31 yards earlier in overtime, but the Colts responded with a field goal of their own to extend the night. That gave Mahomes and the Chiefs one final possession.

Mahomes finished 32 of 47 for 382 yards and three touchdowns, finding Travis Kelce , Xavier Worthy and Jalen Royals for scores. Royals' touchdown was the first of his NFL career and came on fourth down. Kelce caught nine passes for 101 yards, while Worthy scored his first touchdown of the season.

Kenneth Walker III gave Kansas City another major weapon. The running back rushed for 117 yards and added 61 receiving yards, finishing with 178 yards from scrimmage. Mahomes still had to provide the late-game answers.

Mahomes delivers when Chiefs need him most

The Chiefs never established enough control to put Indianapolis away during regulation. Jonathan Taylor rushed for 92 yards and two touchdowns while adding 40 receiving yards. Daniel Jones completed enough timely throws to keep the Colts in position to win, finishing with 210 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception.

Indianapolis even received another opportunity when an apparent Laquon Treadwell fumble was overturned because officials determined he was down by contact. Kansas City refused to panic.

Mahomes continued attacking downfield and connected with Tyquan Thornton for a 45-yard completion that immediately changed the field. He also leaned on Kelce during the most important possessions of the night.

The Colts knew where the ball was going. They simply could not produce one final stop.

Mahomes' 382 yards represented the volume of his performance. His command of the final possessions showed its actual value. Butker handled the rest.

The veteran kicker made four field goals, including both Kansas City scores during overtime. His 40-yard winner dropped through the uprights as the clock expired, preventing Indianapolis from receiving another opportunity.

Chiefs show familiar resilience in overtime

Kansas City did not play a perfect game. The Chiefs allowed Indianapolis to score 30 points, struggled to create separation and needed two overtime possessions to finish the job. Those issues will give Andy Reid plenty to address before Week 3.

The response should still concern the rest of the NFL.

Kansas City survived because Mahomes remained composed, Kelce delivered a vintage performance, Walker supplied balance and Butker converted every important opportunity.

Indianapolis fell to 0-2 and extended its losing streak to nine games dating to last season. The Colts were competitive enough to make the result especially painful. They pushed the Chiefs beyond regulation, responded to Kansas City's first overtime field goal and came within one defensive stop of leaving Arrowhead Stadium with an upset.

Mahomes' quote was simple, but it captured the difference between the teams. Indianapolis fought long enough to create a legitimate chance.

Kansas City fought until there was no time left.
